Op 27 November 1560 is Sotegen Van Den Houte van Gent, Holland, vanweë haar geloof in die Here Jesus Christus gemartel. Voor haar sterwe was haar man ook vir sy geloof gemartel. Tydens haar gevangenisstyd het sy verskeie uitgebreide briewe aan haar drie jeugjarige kinders geskryf. Die volgende is verkorte uittreksels uit daardie briewe wat in volle teks te vinde is op bladsye 646–651 in die Martyr’s Mirror.

Genade, vrede en goedertierenheid van God die Vader en die Here Jesus Christus aan my dierbare kinders, David, Betgen en Tanneken. Hierdie affektueuse groet, deur julle moeder in boeie geskryf, is ’n gedenkteken van die waarheid aan julle. Ek hoop om met die hulp van die Allerhoogste deur my woorde, my lewe en my dood tot hierdie Waarheid te getuig. Mag die wysheid van die Heilige Gees julle onderrig en versterk, sodat julle in die weë van die Here opgevoed mag word. Aangesien dit die Here behaag om my uit hierdie wêreld te neem, laat ek vir julle hierdie herinnering van my geloof in die enigste ware God, nie van silwer of goud nie want sulke juwele bederflik is.

Aanvaar vermaning. Eerstens verman ek julle, my meeste geliefde kinders, laat julle altyd deur dié wat die HERE vrees onderrig. Solank julle goeie vermaning en onderrig gehoorsaam, sal God julle Vader wees en julle nie as wees agterlaat nie. Want David sê: Wie is die mens wat die HERE vrees? hom sal Hy onderrig in die weg wat hy moet kies –Psalm 25:12. Kinders, bedroef nie wanneer julle gekorregeer word nie en spreek nie in toorn tot diegene wat julle verman nie. ’n Wyse seun luister na die vermaning van sy vader: maar ’n verhulder hoor nie bestraffing nie – Spreuke 13:1.

Behoed julle tong. My dierbare kinders, behoed julle tong, sodat dit geen kwaad spreek nie. Bedryf nie bedriegery of kwaadpraat in julle lippe nie. Paulus leer ons om met almal liefdevol en in vrede te lewe as dit moontlik is. –sien 1 Petrus 3:10 en Romeine 12:18. As daar onvriendelik teen julle gepraat word, leer om vriendelik te antwoord, en julle sal deur almal gelief wees. Nederigheid en sagmoedigheid is aangenaam voor beide God en mense.

Liegende lippe is ’n gruwel vir die HERE: maar dié wat trou betoon, is Sy welbehae –Spreuke 12:22. Ek verman julle om op te pas vir leuen, aangesien leuenaars geen deel in die koninkryk van God het nie. –sien Openbaring 21:8.

Wees ywerig in werk en gee aalmoese. Wees altyd ywerig om julle werk te doen, waar julle ook al is; want Paulus sê …want as iemand nie wil werk nie, moet hy ook nie eet nie –2 Tessalonisense 3:10. Dit is ook geskrywe, wees ywerig om te werk, sodat julle …iets het om aan die behoeftige te gee –Efesiërs 4:28.

Dra nie julle gesig weg van die armes nie. Wie sy ore toekan vir die geroep van die arme, homself sal hy ook roep, maar hy sal nie gehoor word nie –Spreuke 21:13. Daarom wees ywerig in gebed, en liefhê die armes; want Christus was ook armes ter wille van ons—Want julle ken die genade van onse Here Jesus Christus, dat al het Hy ryk was, tog ter wille van julle arm geword het, opdat julle deur sy armoede ryk moes word –2 Korintiërs 8:9. Wees daarom ook barmhartig, net soos julle hemelse Vader barmhartig is; want sulkes sal geseënd word en barmhartigheid ontvang. –sien Matteus 5:7.

Beter is ’n bietjie met die vrese van die HERE as ’n groot skat en die moeite daarmee –Spreuke 15:16. En, Beter is ’n droë hap en daardie rustigheid daarmee as ’n huis vol offerandes met twis –Spreuke 17:1. Kies om julle brood te verdien deur die arbeid van julle hande, en om julle brood met vrede te eet. Streef nie daarna om ’n koopman te wees nie, en wees nie ongerus oor groot wins nie.

Wees sagmoedig, barmhartig en rein van hart. Leer om sagmoedig en nederig van hart te wees, want sulkes is geseënd en sal die aarde erf. Wees dan barmhartig, soos julle Vader ook barmhartig is. Lukas 6:36. En, Geseënd is die sagmoediges: want hulle sal die aarde beërwe –Matteus 5:5. Ten slotte, Geseënd is die reines van hart: want hulle sal God sien –Matteus 5:8. Daarom, my dierbare kinders, laat geen onreine gedagtes in julle harte bly nie. Besig julle met psalms, lofsange en geestelike liedere en bose gedagtes sal geen ruimte hê nie. –sien Efesiërs 5:19.

Laat ook nie vuilheid uit julle mond voortvloei nie. Julle sal rekenskap moet gee van alle vuil praat. –sien Matteus 12:36-37. Agterenters julleself altyd as die minste en wees nie wys in julle eie insig nie. Laat julle deur ouerlinge onderrig en wees altyd stil wanneer ander praat. Verneder julle, want …wie homself verhef, sal verneder word; en wie homself verneder, sal verhef word –Matteus 23:12. Want Christus wat die grootste is, het Homself die minste gemaak as ’n voorbeeld vir ons. –sien Johannes 13:13-15.

Vermy ’n luukse lewe. My kinders, begeer nie die luukshede van fyn kos of wyn nie. Hy wat duur feesgeregte begeer sal nie ryk word nie. Wees tevrede met die arbeid van julle hande. Wees nie ’n las vir enigiemand nie solank as wat julle die noodsaaklike dinge kan bekom—…Dit is meer geseënd om te gee as om te ontvang –Handelinge 20:35. Paulus sê: Maar as ons voedsel en bedekking het, sal ons daarmee tevrede wees –1 Timoteus 6:8.

Wees sober en dankbaar soos julle my gehoor het lees van Daniël, Sadrag, Mesjak en Abednego. Hulle is deur die koning van Babilon uitgekies om gevoed te word met dieselfde wyn en kos wat die koning aan sy tafel gedrink en geëet het. Maar hulle het gekies om groentes en water te neem. Hulle wou die wette en gebooie van hul vader volg met soberheid en dankbaarheid in die vrees van God. Uiteindelik was hulle welgevomer en beter as diegene wat van die koning se lekkernye geëet het, sien Daniël hoofstuk 1. So het hulle getrou in die weë van die Here geloop. Hulle het hulle aanvaarbaar gemaak voor God in gebed en smeking, daarom het Hy groot dinge deur hulle gedoen. Hy het hulle uit die leeuwenkuil en uit die brandende oond bevry.

Toe Josef na Egipte verkoop is, het hy geen wêreldse lekkernye begeer nie. Toe die Egiptiese vrou hom verlei wou, het hy God gevrees, en God het hom bewaar. Hy behaag God in soberheid en gebed en God het hom voorsien om heerser oor Egipte te wees. –sien Genesis hoofstukke 37, 39 en 41. Neem ’n voorbeeld hiervan in julle jeug en julle sal God behaag. Hy sal julle van alle verleiding bewaar.

O my lammertjies, julle is nog in jul jeug, tog het julle ’n deel in julle Vader se koninkryk. Sien toe dat julle dit goed bewaar en nie soos Esau nie wat sy erfdeel of geboortereg vir ’n bord potage gee, en sy vader se seën veronagsaam het. –sien Genesis 25:30-34. Maar Jakob het die beter gedeelte gekies en het in die weë van die Here geloop met alle geregtigheid.

Vermy wêreldse lewe. Geniet nie die kwaad van die wêreld soos leuen, bedrog, dobbel, bankette, spel, vloek, vervloeking, kwaadspraak, haat en dans nie, ook nie afgunst, dronkenskap, oordreweheid, afgodediens, gierigheid, wellus, ijdelheid, vuil praat nie. Al oorweeg die wêreld hierdie dinge nie as sonde nie maar noem dit vermaak, tog is hulle gruwels in die oë van die Here. –sien 1 Petrus 4:3-4. As julle genot neem in hierdie dinge verkoop julle julle geboortereg (of die geestelike erfenis) van julle Vader vir ’n brei potage—naamlik vir ’n paar tydelike plesiertjies, wat julle tot verdoemenis lei.

Kies om verdrukking met die kinders van God te ly. Van die tyd van Abel tot vandag is baie verdruk en het gely. Hulle is verwerp, veracht, vervolg en gedood omdat hulle nie die goddelose wêreld en haar valse profete wou volg nie.

My kinders, kies …eerder om verdrukking met die mense van God te ly [sodat julle saam met hulle beloond mag word], as om die genieting van sondige plesier vir ’n tyd –Hebreërs 11:25. Aan sulkes behoort al die lieflike beloftes van God. Dit is geskrywe: …gelyk julle sal huil en kla, maar die wêreld sal bly: en julle sal bedroef wees, maar julle droefheid sal in vreugde verander word –Johannes 16:20. En, Vrees niks van wat julle sal ly: kyk, die duiwel sal sommiges van julle in die gevangenis werp, dat julle beproef mag word; en julle sal tien dae verdrukking hê: wees getrou tot die dood, en Ek sal julle die kroon van die lewe gee –Openbaring 2:10. Ten slotte, Hierin het Ek tot julle gepraat, dat julle in My vrede mag hê. In die wêreld het julle verdrukking; maar moenie moed verloor nie; Ek het die wêreld oorwin –Johannes 16:33.

Instruksies aan my seun, David. David, my dierbare seun, ek beveel jou aan by die Here. Jy is die oudste; leer wysheid, sodat jy ’n goed voorbeeld vir jou susters mag wees. Pas op vir slegte geselskap en om in die straat met slegte seuns te speel. Leer ywerig lees en skryf sodat jy insig mag verkry.

Hê mekaar lief sonder twis of bakleiery. Wees sag vir julle susters. Dra hulle as die swakkeres en help uit liefde alles wat julle kan. Help hulle uit broerlike liefde.

Leer om julle ouerlinge in die goeie te gehoorsaam. Wees ywerig sodat mense julle sal liefhê. Verman mekaar tot goeie werke, beskeidenheid, eerbaarheid en stilheid. Sorg altyd vir mekaar want die tyd het gekom dat …die ongerechtigheid sal oorvloedig word, die liefde van die meeste sal koud word –Matteus 24:12.

Pas op vir bedrog. Onthou, Jesus het gesê …dat, indien dit moontlik was, hulle selfs die uitverkorenes sal bedrieg –Matteus 24:24. Leer om die Skrifte deeglik na te vors sodat julle nie mislei word nie. Glo nie gerugte nie maar ondersoek die saak.

Maak geen rumoer wanneer julle laster besig word nie, maar dra dit ter wille van Christus. Hê julle vyande lief en bid vir diegene wat kwaad van julle praat en julle verdruk. Ly verdrukking eerder as om ander te verdruk. Dra smaad eerder as om ander te smaadmaak. Laat julle laster eerder as dat julle ander laster.

Julle moet voortdurend sorg dat julle nie slegs julle eie wins soek nie, maar altyd sorg vir diegene met wie julle sake doen, of hulle nou jonk of oud is.

Instruksies aan my dogters Betgen en Tanneken, my geliefde lammertjies, ek verman julle in al hierdie selfde dinge, dat julle die gebooie van die Here gehoorsaam. Gehoorsaam ook julle ouerlinge en almal wat julle in deugd onderrig.

Wees ywerig om julle werk te doen, en julle sal geliefd wees waar julle ook al woon. Moet nie ruig, praatgierig, losbesonke, trots of nors van spraak wees nie. Wees vriendelik, eerbaar en stil, soos dit ’n jong meisie betaam.

Bid die Here vir wysheid, en dit sal aan julle gegee word. Leer ywerig lees en skryf, en vind vreugde daarin, en julle sal wys word. Neem plesier en sing psalms, lofsange en geestelike liedere. Leer om die Here van julle jeugd af te behaag, soos die heilige vroue en maagde van ouds. Ester was ook ’n maagd wat God vrees; sy was beklee met nederigheid, was aangenaam, eerbaar, goedhartig en nederig van hart; daarom bekoor sy Koning Ahasveros meer as al die ander maagde. –sien Ester 2:17. Maar selfs in haar hoë rang was sy nie trots nie. Al het sy gestraal in koninklike kleding, het sy haar hart verneder met vas en gebed tot die Here, vir haar broeders, sodat hulle uit die hande van hul vyande verlos kon word. Sy het haar nie meer ag gesien as een van die minstes van haar broeders nie.

Wanneer julle die ouderdom van insig bereik het, sien toe dat julle julle tooi met die werke van die Gees soos goedheid, sagmoedigheid, nederigheid, gehoorsaamheid, lankmoedigheid, geregtigheid, beskeidenheid, eerbaarheid, reinheid, vredeliewendheid, standvastigheid, barmhartigheid, wysheid, ywer in goeie werke, geloof, hoop en liefde. Hê God bo alles in die wêreld lief en doen aan julle naaste soos julle wil hê mense aan julle moet doen. –sien Galasiërs 5:22-23 en Titus 2:3-5. Onthou dat Jesus gesê het: …Gij zult die Here u God liefhê met al u hart, en met al u siel, en met al u verstand. Dit is die eerste en grootste gebod. En die tweede is hom gelyk: Gij zult u naaste liefhê soos u self. Aan hierdie twee gebooie hang die hele wet en die profete –Matteus 22:37-40.

Laat ons bly wees en juig, en Hom eer gee: want die bruilof van die Lam het gekom, en sy bruid het haar klaargemaak. En aan haar was gegee dat sy met fyn linne beklee moes word, suiwer en wit: want die fyn linne is die geregtigheid van die heiliges –Openbaring 19:7-8. My dogters, dit is die tooi van die heiliges; werk aan so ’n trourok, sodat julle in die bruilof van die Lam kan inkom, waar die wat …die regverdiges, [sal] skyn soos die son in die koninkryk van hul Vader… –Matteus 13:43. Mag die Here julle lei soos Hy Israel uit Egipte gelei het, en julle na die Nuwe Jerusalem bring, dat ons mekaar met vreugde mag sien op die dag van die opstanding. Ek beveel julle aan by die Here, die God van Abraham, die God van Isak en die God van Jakob; mag Hy julle bewaar tot die einde van julle lewens.

Ten slotte, O my dierbare kinders, ek het dit in trane geskryf, julle uit liefde vermanend. My gebed en sorg is voortdurend vir julle heil. Ek hoop en bid voortdurend dat Hy, in Sy barmhartigheid, julle sal bewaar, soos Hy Josef, Moses en Daniël bewaar het te midde van goddelose mense. En Hy sal dit doen indien julle ywer toon om die waarheid te volg.

Dit is my laaste vaarwel, my dierbare lammertjies. Onthou mekaar altyd in liefde; leer ywerig om te lees en te skryf en gehoorsaam almal in die goeie. Ek neem afskeid, my dierbare kinders Betgen, David en Tanneken. Afskeid aan al my dierbare broers en susters, en vriende oral.

Geskryf deur my, Sotegen Van Den Houte, julle moeder in boeie; geskryf in haastigheid (terwyl ek van die koue bewe), uit liefde vir julle almal, amen.

Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created –Revelation 4:11.

This hymn, often called the “National Anthem of Christendom,” is perhaps one of the greatest of hymns of all time. It was written by Edward Perronet, first appearing in the November 1779 issue of Gospel Magazine. It was edited by Augustus Toplady, who is also the author of another well-known hymn, “Rock of Ages”. The text of this hymn, All Hail the Power of Jesus Name, has been translated into almost every language where Christianity is known. Wherever it is sung, it communicates to the spiritual needs of human hearts. One writer has said, “So long as there are Christians on earth, it will continue to be sung; and after that, in heaven.”

Edward Perronet was born at Sundridge, Kent, England, in 1726. He was a descendant of a distinguished French Huguenot family who had fled to Switzerland and later to England because of the religious persecution in France. Edward’s father, a pastor in the State Church of England, was strongly sympathetic with the evangelical movement spearheaded by the Wesleys and George Whitefield. Edward, too, like his father, became a minister in the Anglican Church but was always critical of its ways. Once he wrote, “I was born and I am likely to die in the tottering communion of the Church of England, but I despise her nonsense.” Soon, however, he broke from the Church and threw himself strenuously into the evangelistic endeavors of the Wesleys during the 1740s and 1750s.

Charles Wesley writes of Edward Perronet’s boldness in preaching. At one time he and Perronet were beset in a house by a mob of rough revilers, whom Perronet opposed courageously, while they abused him and threw dirt on him. It was during this time that the Wesleys and their followers suffered much persecution and even violence from those who disagreed with their ministry. Concerning these experiences, Wesley made the following notation in his diary: “From Rockdale we went to Bolton, and soon found that the Rockdale lions were lambs in comparison with those of Bolton.” Edward Perronet was thrown down and rolled in mud and mire. Stones were hurled and windows broken.

Another interesting account is given regarding the relationship between the Wesleys and Perronet. John Wesley wanted to hear Perronet preach, and he, being 18 years younger than John had always refused to preach in the older churchman’s presence. So, one day Wesley seeing Edward in the congregation announced that he would preach at the next service. Desiring to avoid a public conflict with Wesley, Perronet mounted the pulpit the next morning, but quickly explained that he had never consented to preach. “However,” he added, “I shall deliver the greatest sermon that has ever been preached on earth.” He then read the Sermon on the Mount and sat down without comment.

After eight years of co-operation with the Wesleys, Perronet’s strong-mindedness and free spirit caused a division between them, as he disagreed with some of their regulations. They continued, however, to esteem and love each other.

The last years of Perronet were spent at Canterbury, where he was pastor of an independent church, and where he died in 1792, at the age of sixty-six. His last words have also become a classic: “Glory to God in the height of His divinity! Glory to God in the depth of His humanity! Glory to God in His all-sufficiency! Into His hands I commend my spirit.”

Though Perronet wrote many other hymns and forms of poetry, none of them, have attained fame except the immortal “All Hail the Power of Jesus Name.” The success of this text has, no doubt, been furthered by three fine tunes. “Coronation,” composed by Oliver Holden, a Massachusetts carpenter, self-taught musician, and respected singing-school teacher, is most widely used in America. “Miles Lane” composed by William Shrubsole, Perronet’s personal friend, is the most popular in Great Britain. While the festive “Diadem” tune, composed in 1838 for this text by James Ellor, an English layman, is frequently used as a choir number. This hymn was originally written having the title, “On the Resurrection,” and there were eight stanzas, as follows:

All hail the power of Jesus’ name,
Let angels prostrate fall
Bring forth the royal diadem,
To crown Him Lord of all!

Let high born seraphs tune the lyre,
And, as they tune it, fall
Before His face who tunes their choir,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye morning stars of light,
Who fixed this floating ball,
Now hail the Strength of Israel’s might,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God,
Who from His altar call;
Extol the stem of Jesse’s rod,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Ye seed of Israel’s chosen race,
Ye ransomed of the fall,
Hail Him who saves you by His grace
And crown Him Lord of all!

Hail Him, ye heirs of David’s line,
Whom David Lord did call.
The God incarnate, Man divine,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Sinners, whose love can ne’er forget
The wormwood and the gall,
Go spread your trophies at His feet,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Let every tribe and every tongue
That bound creation’s call
Now shout in universal song,
The crowned Lord of all!

As it now stands in our hymnbooks, the hymn is shortened and changed, and one stanza has been added by the famous hymn collector, Rev. John Rippon, in 1787.

Oh, that with yonder sacred throng
We at His feet may fall;
We’ll join the everlasting song,
And crown Him Lord of all.

As we wrap up this amazing story of the life of Edward Perronet and the others who have had their part in bringing this immortal hymn to us, let’s take a look in closing at the effect this hymn has had on heathens who knew nothing about Jesus. The most famous story connected with Perronet’s great hymn is told of the missionary to India, Rev. E.P. Scott. One day he saw on the street a man of so strange an appearance that he inquired about him and learned that he belonged to a wild mountain tribe among whom Christ had never been preached. Mr. Scott prayed over the matter and decided to visit that tribe. As soon as he reached their mountain home, he fell in among a savage band of murderous tribesmen who were on a war expedition, and who were closing in on him with their spears. They seized him and pointed their spears at his heart. At once the missionary drew out the violin that he always carried with him and began to play and sing in the native language, “All hail the power of Jesus’ name!” He closed his eyes, expecting death at any minute. When he reached the fourth stanza, and nothing had happened, he opened his eyes, and was amazed to see that the spears had fallen from the hands of the savages, and big tears were in their eyes! They invited Mr. Scott to their homes, and he spent the remaining years of his life preaching and ministering God’s love and redemption to these people. God in His providence used a simple hymn as a means of introducing the gospel to a group of needy pagans.

U iswaardig, Here, om heerlikheid en eer en krag te ontvang: want U het alle dinge geskape, en om U wil het hulle bestaan en is geskape – Openbaring 4:11.

Hierdie gesang, dikwels die “Nasionale Volkslied van die Christendom” genoem, is miskien een van die grootste liedere van alle tye. Dit is deur Edward Perronet geskryf en verskyn die eerste keer in die November 1779-uitgawe van Gospel Magazine. Dit is geredigeer deur Augustus Toplady, wat ook die skrywer is van ’n ander bekende gesang, “Rock of Ages”. Die teks van hierdie gesang, All Hail the Power of Jesus Name, is in byna elke taal vertaal waar Christusendom bekend is. Waar dit ook al gesing word, spreek dit die geestelike behoeftes van mense se harte aan. Een skrywer het gesê: “Solank daar Christene op aarde is, sal dit aanhou gesing word; en daarna, in die hemel.”

Edward Perronet is in 1726 by Sundridge, Kent, Engeland gebore. Hy was ’n afstammeling van ’n vooraanstaande Franse Hugenote-familie wat na Switserland en later na Engeland gevlug het weens die godsdienstige vervolging in Frankryk. Edward se vader, ’n predikant in die State Church of England, was sterk simpatiek met die evangeliese beweging wat deur die Wesleys en George Whitefield aangevoer is. Edward het, soos sy vader, ook ’n predikant in die Anglikaanse Kerk geword, maar was altyd kritiek op haar maniere. Eenkeer het hy geskryf: “Ek is gebore en waarskynlik sal ek in die wankelende gemeenskap van die Church of England sterf, maar ek minag haar nonsens.” Binnekort het hy egter van die Kerk losgemaak en hom kragtig in die evangeliserende bedrywighede van die Wesleys in die 1740’s en 1750’s gewerp.

Charles Wesley skryf van Edward Perronet se moedigheid in prediking. Op een stadium is hy en Perronet in ’n huis deur ’n skare van ruwe lasteraars aangeval, wat Perronet dapper teëgestaan het terwyl hulle hom beledig en met modder bedek het. Dit was in hierdie tyd dat die Wesleys en hul volgelinge baie vervolging en selfs geweld van diegene wat nie met hul bediening saamgestem het nie, ervaar het. Oor hierdie ervarings het Wesley die volgende aantekening in sy dagboek gemaak: “Van Rockdale het ons na Bolton gegaan, en het gou gevind dat die Rockdale-luie lammetjies was in vergelyking met dié van Bolton.” Edward Perronet is neergeslaan en in modder en drab gerol. Stene is gegooi en vensters gebreek.

’n Ander interessante verslag handel oor die verhouding tussen die Wesleys en Perronet. John Wesley wou Perronet hoor preek, en hy, wat 18 jaar jonger as John was, het altyd geweier om in die ouer kerkmans teenwoordigheid te preek. Op ’n dag, toe Wesley Edward in die gemeente sien, het hy aangekondig dat hy by die volgende diens sal preek. Om ’n openbare konflik met Wesley te vermy, het Perronet die volgende oggend die kansel bestyg, maar vinnig verduidelik dat hy nooit ingestem het om te preek nie. “Tog,” het hy bygevoeg, “ek sal die grootste preek doen wat nog ooit op aarde gepreek is.” Hy het toe die Bergrede gelees en sonder kommentaar gaan sit.

Na agt jaar van samewerking met die Wesleys, het Perronet se stewige geaardheid en vrye gees ’n skeiding tussen hulle veroorsaak, omdat hy met sommige van hul regulasies verskil het. Hulle het egter voortgegaan om mekaar te ag en lief te hê.

Die laaste jare van Perronet is in Canterbury deurgebring, waar hy predikant van ’n onafhanklike kerk was, en waar hy in 1792 op sestig-en-sesjarige ouderdom gesterf het. Sy laaste woorde het ook ’n klassieke status verkry: “Eer aan God in die hoogte van Sy godheid! Eer aan God in die diepte van Sy mensheid! Eer aan God in Sy algenoegsaamheid! In Sy hande beveel ek my gees aan.”

Alhoewel Perronet baie ander gesange en vorme van poësie geskryf het, het geen van hulle roem verwerf behalwe die onsterflike “All Hail the Power of Jesus Name.” Die sukses van hierdie teks is, sonder twyfel, verder bevorder deur drie uitstekende melodieë. “Coronation,” deur Oliver Holden gekomponeer — ’n Massachusetts-houtbewerker, selfopgeleide musikant en gerespekteerde sangskoolonderwyser — word in Amerika die wydste gebruik. “Miles Lane,” gekomponeer deur William Shrubsole, Perronet se persoonlike vriend, is die gewildste in Groot-Brittanje. Terwyl die feestelike “Diadem”-melodie, in 1838 vir hierdie teks deur James Ellor, ’n Engelse lekmens, gekomponeer, dikwels as ’n koornommer gebruik word. Hierdie gesang is oorspronklik onder die titel “On the Resurrection” geskryf en het agt stanzaʼs gehad, soos volg:

Ere aan die Naam van Jesus toe!
Laat engele nederig val,
Bring die koninklike diadeem voort,
Om Hom te kroon, Here van almal!

Laat hooggeborene serafe die lier stem,
En terwyl hulle dit stem, val neer
Voor Sy aangesig wat hul koor stem,
En kroon Hom, Here van almal!

Kroon Hom, o ogendsterre van lig,
Wat hierdie wentelende wêreld vasgestel het,
Groet nou die Krag van Israël se mag,
En kroon Hom, Here van almal!

Kroon Hom, o martelare van julle God,
Wat van Sy altaar roep;
Verhef die stam van Jesse se riet,
En kroon Hom, Here van almal!

Julle, saad van Israel se uitverkore ras,
Julle, wat van die val verlos is,
Eer Hom wat julle deur Sy genade red,
En kroon Hom, Here van almal!

Eer Hom, erfgename van Dawid se nageslag,
Wie Dawid as Here geroep het.
Die God wat mens geword het, die goddelike Mens,
En kroon Hom, Here van almal!

Sondares, wie se liefde nooit kan vergeet
Die erdwurg en die gal nie,
Gaan versprei julle trofeë aan Sy voete uit,
En kroon Hom, Here van almal!

Laat elke stam en elke tong
Wat die geskape wêreld gebind het
Nou uitroep in ’n universele lied,
Die gekroonde Here van almal!

Soos dit nou in ons liedboeke staan, is die gesang verkort en verander, en een stanza is deur die beroemde liederversamelaar, ds. John Rippon, in 1787 bygevoeg.

O dat ons met daardie heilige skare
By Sy voete mag val;
Ons sal by die ewige lied aansluit,
En Hom kroon, Here van almal.

Terwyl ons hierdie wonderlike verhaal van Edward Perronet se lewe en van die ander wat hul deel gehad het om hierdie onsterflike gesang aan ons te bring afsluit, kom ons in afsluiting kyk na die uitwerking wat hierdie gesang op heidene gehad het wat niks van Jesus geweet het nie. Die bekendste verhaal wat met Perronet se groot gesang verbind word, word vertel van die predikant in Indië, ds. E.P. Scott. Op ’n dag het hy ’n man in die straat gesien van so vreemde voorkoms dat hy oor hom navraag gedoen en verneem het dat hy tot ’n wilde bergstam behoort waartydens Christus nog nooit verkondig is nie. Mnr. Scott het oor die saak gebid en besluit om die stam te besoek. Sodra hy hul berghuis bereik het, het hy onder ’n woeste bende moorddadige stamlede geval wat op ’n oorlogstog was en wat met hul spiesse op hom toegesluit het. Hulle het hom gegryp en hul spiesse na sy hart gerig. Dadelik het die sendeling die viool uitgehaal wat hy altyd by hom gedra het en begin speel en sing in die plaaslike taal, “Ere aan die Naam van Jesus toe!” Hy het sy oë toegemaak en verwag om enige oomblik te sterf. Toe hy by die vierde stanza kom en niks gebeur het nie, het hy sy oë oopgemaak en was verbaas om te sien dat die spiesse uit die hande van die wredees geval het, en groot trane in hul oë was! Hulle het mnr. Scott na hul huise uitgenooi, en hy het die oorblywende jare van sy lewe daarmee bestee om hierdie mense die evangelie en God se liefde en verlossing voor te hou. God het in Sy voorsienigheid ’n eenvoudige gesang as ’n middel gebruik om die evangelie aan ’n groep behoeftige heidene bekend te stel.

Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock to the backside of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, even to Horeb –Exodus 3:1.

The back side of the desert has long been understood as God’s school wherewith He has instructed many of His servants, of whom Moses stands chief. At the prime age of 40, he found himself …learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds. And when he was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel –Acts 7:22-23.

I have no doubt that God can, and does, use men of great ability, capacity, and training, but spiritual leadership requires an ingredient that is not derived from doing, attaining, and accomplishing. The bane of the zealot is often too little confidence in God and too much confidence in the flesh. This pride and restlessness is not dealt with in a seminary nor is it normally exterminated during vigilant duty. For many of God’s servants, it is extracted from the soul on the soil of deserted sands. This arid and abandoned acreage that appears void of life and fruitfulness is where many servants learn to put their face in the dust and yield to what may seem to be inactivity, unfruitfulness, and rejection.

Moses’ life could be divided into three sections. He spent his first forty years learning the wisdom of Egypt, the next forty as a shepherd in Midian, and a final forty as the shepherd of Israel. We can imagine that the first third of his pilgrimage was filled with tremendous activity, advancement, and accomplishment. It had undoubtedly been rehearsed to him that at his birth he …was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months –Acts 7:20.

The miraculous river rescue by Pharoah’s daughter would serve to confirm that he was destined to be an instrument of God’s divine orchestration. As a centerpiece of national attention, it is certainly understandable how this man who …was mighty in words and in deeds –Acts 7:22, was brimming with self-confidence in his ability to accomplish God’s bidding.

In today’s economy, Moses would be esteemed as the ideal candidate for church leadership. He was in every way qualified. He stood above his countrymen in education, and he possessed above-normal natural, financial, and spiritual endowments. He had emerged from the “University” of Egypt as a man mighty in word and deed and he had an obvious call from God upon his life. He was a conservative man who chose …rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season –Hebrews 11:25.

Still, amidst all his fine credentials he was yet deficient for the work that God had called him to. And so, God conveniently conducted him into the land of Midian to enroll him in another school to feed upon the bitter herbs of disappointment and rejection, obscurity and loneliness, and unfulfilled dreams and longings. While it was his earlier ambition to voluntarily align himself with the people of God, this chapter of his life was enacted by compulsion.

We learn from the account in Exodus that the latter third of his life was loaded with intricate involvement and major ministry. While the exit from Egypt is an exciting read and provides great insight, most of us cannot honestly relate to the mighty Moses and his dynamic coalition with God. Rather, it is the uneventful 40-year mid-section of his life that many of us find ourselves in. Though there are but a few dozen verses that represent these four decades of his life, we assume that it was a thorough schooling that inscribed immense patience, soul searching, and perhaps a bit of frustration.

For us, it represents a period when the parched sands of time about us seem to be producing nothing more fruitful than a revelation of our dry, crusty heart—shriveled and wasted by the consequences of our failures and past sins. It is at these times that we can have a lapse in faith, not that we blame God for our circumstances, but that we may begin to see our lives as futile, and that each day is the same as the previous one. Perhaps we begin to walk around in a visionless stupor—through a fog of spiritual depression—as we grope for encouragement and a reminder that God has not forgotten us. At times, it even seems that our prayers hit the ceiling and bounce back, laughing and lying to us in grim mockery that our usefulness in the Kingdom of God is over. During extended times of trials and testing, we can feel abandoned. We can even imagine that God has turned against us. We look up to Heaven and ask, “Why Lord?” We will never experience rejection and being forsaken to the extent that the Lord Jesus did, but when we experience them in our petty little realm, it seems to sap all our spiritual strength and vigor. We think… If the Lord should require forty years of this from us there would be no time left in our lives to capitalize on what we have learned. But God’s timing is perfect. Thus, it behooves us to not concern ourselves so much with the longevity of our schooling, but to be thoroughly acquainted with the message from Midian. While some receive the bitter strokes of Midian and retreat to stand cynically on the sidelines, we must shake off the dust of the desert and arise with an understanding of…

God’s Purpose

God has a purpose for every detail of our lives. He may plant us in a difficult position, to forge in us a new vocation. It was alone in Midian where Moses learned of his own pride, self-confidence, lack of faith, and the utter folly that his own hands had participated in. Here in his Midian, he was alone and yet not alone; numerous other saints have joined him there. The sons of Jacob and the wife of Potiphar sent another vibrant servant there—Joseph. The wild rage of a jealous king sent a gifted young harpist there. Even an old and foolish king who refused to be taught found himself in a wilderness eating grass like an ox until he recanted of his pride.

Throughout the pages of history, countless saints have realized that ‘the darker the valley, the more I learned to pray’. While they arrive at the threshold of the new day loaded down with bountiful exuberance, they are soon stripped naked in a metamorphic change and finally emerge with nothing but the rod of God in their hands. Gone are the days when they were swift to speak, swift to act, and slow to hear. In Midian, the student learns to shift his focus from, “I will do great things for God” to “What wilt thou have me to do?”

And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do –Acts 9:6. The new arrivals in Midian have many answers, but most of them involve a one-act-play with self as the main character. The graduates walk out silent and sober, for they’ve come through the arduous process of separating the flesh from the spirit which was accomplished by…

God’s Purging

The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the LORD trieth the hearts –Proverbs 17:3. As Moses passed through the gates of Midian, the first scene that God set before his eyes was an injustice at a well. Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters… –Exodus 2:16, who were being driven away by a band of uncouth shepherds. But Moses had been well trained in every dimension of Egyptian plutocracy, which would have included all aspects of military expertise and worldly leadership skills. Thus, when he stepped in to assist the helpless shepherdesses, he would have been quite capable to do so. These daughters of the priest of Midian appreciated the help which they recounted to their father that …An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock –Exodus 2:19. Upon hearing this tale, their father, Reuel, was so impressed that he gave Moses a reception, a job, and a wife… all in one verse. –see Exodus 2:21.

…Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them –Mark 10:42. While Moses’ quest for justice may have been noble, his orientation was merely Gentile. This may work for establishing pecking order in a hen house, but it is destined for failure in leading forth the people of God. But … whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister: And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all –Mark 10:43-44.

This doctrine was foreign to Egypt and to Moses as well. Many good and talented men can successfully operate a business using Gentile authority, but it rarely works in their home, and it is even more futile in a church. Thus, God moved His chosen vessel from royalty to proletariat (the working class), almost overnight. He is then given a job which was loathed by the people who had trained him—…for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians –Genesis 46:34. This fining pot is not just to teach us a much-needed lesson, but to guide us into…

God’s Provision

The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way –Psalm 25:9. God will never abandon us on the back side of the desert; instead, He tailors our life circumstances to bring us into His fullness. If we resist the temptation to espouse an attitude of anger, then God will be able to teach us His ways. But to Moses, the situation presented itself such that God’s divine direction was the last thing he would suspect was happening.

Happening…? It seemed that nothing was happening. The weeks melted into months, the months into years, and the years into decades, all the while the gifted Moses remained an underachieving shepherd. One of the hardest things that we struggle with is “waiting.” Almost every Christian will face a long time of tribulation and we are told to: …think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you –1 Peter 4:12. But we should not judge God’s means by our feeble sense, for in the meantime, the wonderful working of waiting prepares us for…

God’s Promotion

38, 39, … 40 years. Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt –Exodus 3:10.

Perhaps God is enamored with the number 40, but more than likely, it was the time that it took for Moses to land at the seat of resignation. His self-esteem has been fully extinguished, and he humbly asks: …Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt? –Exodus 3:11.

Moses was not less qualified than he was forty years prior to this time, but his presumption had evaporated in the heat of the desert sun. The experience gleaned in the rugged pastures with the stubborn sheep has brought him to the understanding that this will be nearly an impossible feat. But there is no ordained calling issued independently from…

God’s Promise

…Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be a token unto thee, that I have sent thee: When thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain –Exodus 3:12.

Not that Moses had attained perfection, for we find Moses provoking God to anger in the very next chapter—And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses… –Exodus 4:14. Then soon again he is the direct object in the path of God’s sword—And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him –Exodus 4:24. Even so, while his vessel is still made of clay, it has met with a firing that has prepared him for the Lord’s service, and for us God will not revoke His promises in the wind of our whims. Thus, the great I AM THAT I AM –see Exodus 3:14, has laid upon human shoulders the immense and eternal task of leading His people. But this charge is not to be executed without…

God’s Power

What was the real refinement from Moses’ time spent in the desert? We notice his rash willingness to wield the sword before his arrival, but upon his exit, he only bore a rod in his hand. With the sword he had overcome an Egyptian offender, but with the rod he overcame the entire forces of Egypt. The rod of God brought forth the water in the wilderness. It was the rod of God, that, when lifted high by feeble hands secured the victory over Amalek. What is the rod of God? Before his days in Midian, he hardly knew it existed. Forty years later there hardly exists a scene without it.

The rod is the power of God unto salvation. It is the wisdom of God, the truth of God, the testimony of God, but more than all of these it is the chastening of God. Without it, man does not receive nor perceive the love of God for without it man is not connected to God. For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons –Hebrews 12:6-8.

This same Moses, who at one time was willing to exercise lordship (Gentile authority) over God’s people now finds himself entreating God and staying His wrath from destroying them. The people who accused Moses of leading them out to kill them and even at one point were ready to stone him are now at the center of his heart and affection, even though they are at the cause of his failure to enter the promised land. This is the love of Christ. But where is this learned except under the rod of God, on the back side of the desert, in the Egyptian dungeons, in the caves of Adullam, in the straits of Arabia, and in the silent solitude of the back burner where God has ordained that many of His people go until they learn to …learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls –Matthew 11:29. Surely that is where Moses secured the character known to the biblical scholar as the meekest man to walk the face of the earth. Surely there is no more opposite place on earth to learn it but in the school of suffering.

And so here we shall abide as well, so that we …may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death –Philippians 3:10.

Ora Mosè pascolava il gregge di Ietro, suo suocero, sacerdote di Madian; e condusse il gregge dietro il deserto, e venne al monte di Dio, a Horeb –Esodo 3:1.

Il retro del deserto è da tempo inteso come la scuola di Dio nella quale Egli ha istruito molti dei suoi servi, di cui Mosè è il principale. All’età matura di 40 anni, si trovò …istruito di tutta la sapienza degli Egiziani, ed era potente nelle parole e nelle opere. E quando ebbe compiuto quaranta anni, gli venne in cuore di visitare i suoi fratelli, i figli d’Israele –Atti 7:22-23.

Non ho dubbio che Dio possa, e usi, uomini di grande abilità, capacità e formazione, ma la leadership spirituale richiede un ingrediente che non deriva dal fare, conseguire e compiere. Il male dello zelante è spesso avere troppo poca fiducia in Dio e troppa fiducia nella carne. Questo orgoglio e questa irrequietezza non si affrontano in un seminario né normalmente si estirpano durante il servizio vigile. Per molti servi di Dio, esso viene estratto dall’anima nel suolo delle sabbie deserte. Questa terra arida e abbandonata che appare priva di vita e di frutto è dove molti servitori imparano a mettere il volto nella polvere e a cedere a ciò che può sembrare inattività, infertilità e rifiuto.

La vita di Mosè può essere divisa in tre sezioni. Trascorse i suoi primi quaranta anni apprendendo la sapienza dell’Egitto, i successivi quaranta come pastore in Madian, e gli ultimi quaranta come pastore d’Israele. Possiamo immaginare che il primo terzo del suo pellegrinaggio fosse pieno di grande attività, avanzamento e realizzazione. Gli era senza dubbio stato ripetuto che alla sua nascita egli …era bellissimo, e fu nutrito nella casa di suo padre tre mesi –Atti 7:20.

Il miracoloso salvataggio nel fiume da parte della figlia del faraone servì a confermare che era destinato a essere uno strumento dell’orchestrazione divina di Dio. Come centro dell’attenzione nazionale, è certamente comprensibile come quest’uomo che …era potente nelle parole e nelle opere –Atti 7:22, fosse colmo di fiducia in sé nella sua capacità di adempiere il volere di Dio.

Nell’economia odierna, Mosè sarebbe considerato il candidato ideale per la leadership di chiesa. Era sotto ogni aspetto qualificato. Si distingueva tra i suoi connazionali per l’istruzione, e possedeva doni naturali, finanziari e spirituali sopra la norma. Era uscito dall’“Università” d’Egitto come un uomo potente nella parola e nell’opera e aveva una chiamata evidente di Dio sulla sua vita. Era un uomo conservatore che scelse …piuttosto di soffrire afflizione col popolo di Dio, che godere dei piaceri del peccato per un poco –Ebrei 11:25.

Tuttavia, in mezzo a tutti i suoi ottimi titoli era ancora carente per l’opera a cui Dio lo aveva chiamato. E così, Dio convenientemente lo condusse nella terra di Madian per iscriverlo in un’altra scuola dove nutrirsi delle amare erbe della delusione e del rifiuto, dell’oscurità e della solitudine, e dei sogni e desideri non realizzati. Mentre prima era sua ambizione allinearsi volontariamente col popolo di Dio, questo capitolo della sua vita si svolse per costrizione.

Apprendiamo dal racconto in Esodo che l’ultimo terzo della sua vita fu carico di coinvolgimenti intricati e di ministero rilevante. Sebbene l’uscita dall’Egitto sia una lettura eccitante e fornisca grande intuizione, la maggior parte di noi non può onestamente relazionarsi con il possente Mosè e la sua coalizione dinamica con Dio. Piuttosto, è la monotona sezione mediana di 40 anni della sua vita in cui molti di noi si ritrovano. Sebbene vi siano solo poche dozzine di versetti che rappresentano questi quattro decenni della sua vita, supponiamo che sia stata un’istruzione approfondita che ha inciso immensa pazienza, ricerca dell’anima, e forse un po’ di frustrazione.

Per noi rappresenta un periodo in cui le sabbie aride del tempo intorno a noi sembrano produrre nient’altro che la rivelazione del nostro cuore secco e crostoso—avvizzito e sprecato dalle conseguenze dei nostri fallimenti e peccati passati. È in questi momenti che possiamo avere una battuta d’arresto nella fede, non perché biasimiamo Dio per le nostre circostanze, ma perché possiamo iniziare a vedere le nostre vite come inutili, e che ogni giorno è uguale al precedente. Forse cominciamo a camminare in uno stordimento senza visione—attraverso una nebbia di depressione spirituale—mentre brancoliamo per un incoraggiamento e un promemoria che Dio non ci ha dimenticati. A volte, sembra persino che le nostre preghiere urtino il soffitto e rimbalzino indietro, ridendo e mentendo a noi in cupo scherno che la nostra utilità nel Regno di Dio è finita. Durante lunghi periodi di prove e tentazioni, possiamo sentirci abbandonati. Possiamo persino immaginare che Dio si sia rivoltato contro di noi. Alziamo lo sguardo al Cielo e chiediamo: “Perché, Signore?” Non sperimenteremo mai il rifiuto e l’essere abbandonati nella misura in cui li sperimentò il Signore Gesù, ma quando li sperimentiamo nel nostro piccolo regno, sembra prosciugare tutta la nostra forza e vigore spirituale. Pensiamo… Se il Signore dovesse richiederci quaranta anni di questo non rimarrebbe tempo nelle nostre vite per capitalizzare ciò che abbiamo imparato. Ma il tempo di Dio è perfetto. Pertanto, ci conviene non preoccuparci tanto della durata della nostra scuola, ma di essere completamente familiari col messaggio di Madian. Mentre alcuni ricevono i colpi amari di Madian e si ritirano per stare cinicamente ai margini, dobbiamo scrollarci di dosso la polvere del deserto e sorgere con una comprensione di…

Il proposito di Dio

Dio ha uno scopo per ogni dettaglio delle nostre vite. Egli può piantarci in una posizione difficile, per forgiare in noi una nuova vocazione. Fu solo in Madian che Mosè apprese del proprio orgoglio, fiducia in sé, mancanza di fede, e della totale follia a cui le sue mani avevano partecipato. Qui, nel suo Madian, era solo e tuttavia non solo; numerosi altri santi lo hanno raggiunto lì. I figli di Giacobbe e la moglie di Potifar mandarono un altro servo vibrante lì—Giuseppe. La furia selvaggia di un re geloso mandò lì un giovane arpaista dotato. Persino un re vecchio e sciocco che rifiutò di essere ammaestrato si trovò in una desolazione a mangiare erba come un bue finché non rinunciò al suo orgoglio.

Attraverso le pagine della storia, innumerevoli santi hanno realizzato che «più oscura è la valle, più imparo a pregare». Pur arrivando alla soglia del nuovo giorno carichi di esuberanza, sono presto denudati in un cambiamento metamorfico e infine emergono con nient’altro che il bastone di Dio nelle mani. Sono spariti i giorni in cui erano pronti a parlare, pronti ad agire e lenti ad ascoltare. In Madian, lo studente impara a spostare il suo focus da “Farò grandi cose per Dio” a “Che vuoi che io faccia?”

E quello tremando e stupefatto disse: Signore, che vuoi che io faccia? E il Signore gli disse: Alzati e va nella città, e sarà detto a te ciò che devi fare –Atti 9:6. I nuovi arrivati a Madian hanno molte risposte, ma la maggior parte di esse riguardano una pièce in un atto con il sé come personaggio principale. I diplomati escono silenziosi e sobri, poiché sono passati attraverso l’arduo processo di separare la carne dallo spirito che fu compiuto da…

La purificazione di Dio

Il crogiuolo è per l’argento, e il forno per l’oro; ma il Signore mette alla prova i cuori –Proverbi 17:3. Quando Mosè varcò i cancelli di Madian, la prima scena che Dio pose davanti ai suoi occhi fu un’ingiustizia a un pozzo. Ora il sacerdote di Madian aveva sette figlie… –Esodo 2:16, che venivano respinte da una banda di pastori rozzi. Ma Mosè era stato ben istruito in ogni dimensione della plutocrazia egiziana, che avrebbe incluso tutti gli aspetti dell’esperienza militare e delle abilità di leadership mondane. Così, quando intervenne per aiutare le pastorelle indifese, sarebbe stato più che capace di farlo. Queste figlie del sacerdote di Madian apprezzarono l’aiuto al punto che lo riferirono al padre dicendo che …Un Egiziano ci liberò dalla mano dei pastori, e anche attingeva acqua per noi, e diede da bere al gregge –Esodo 2:19. Sentendo questo racconto, il loro padre, Reuel, fu così impressionato che diede a Mosè un’accoglienza, un lavoro e una moglie… il tutto in un verso. –vedi Esodo 2:21.

…Sapete che quelli che sono considerati governare sulle nazioni le dominano; e i loro grandi esercitano potere su di esse –Marco 10:42. Sebbene la ricerca di giustizia di Mosè potesse essere nobile, la sua orientazione era puramente gentile. Questo può funzionare per stabilire l’ordine di supremazia in un pollaio, ma è destinato al fallimento nel condurre il popolo di Dio. Ma… chi vorrà essere grande fra voi, sarà vostro servitore; e chi fra voi sarà il primo, sarà il servo di tutti –Marco 10:43-44.

Questa dottrina era straniera all’Egitto e anche a Mosè. Molti uomini buoni e talentuosi possono gestire con successo un’impresa usando l’autorità gentile, ma raramente funziona nella loro casa, ed è ancor più inutile in una chiesa. Così, Dio spostò il suo vaso scelto dalla regalità al proletariato (la classe lavoratrice), quasi da un giorno all’altro. Gli fu quindi dato un lavoro disprezzato dalle persone che lo avevano formato—…poiché ogni pastore è abominevole agli Egiziani –Genesi 46:34. Questo crogiuolo non è solo per insegnarci una lezione tanto necessaria, ma per guidarci verso…

La provvidenza di Dio

I mansueti egli li guida nel giudizio; egli insegna la sua via agli umili –Salmi 25:9. Dio non ci abbandonerà mai sul retro del deserto; invece, modella le nostre circostanze di vita per portarci nella sua pienezza. Se resistiamo alla tentazione di assumere un atteggiamento di rabbia, allora Dio sarà in grado di insegnarci le sue vie. Ma per Mosè la situazione si presentò in modo che la direzione divina di Dio fosse l’ultima cosa che avrebbe sospettato stesse accadendo.

Che stesse accadendo…? Sembrava che nulla stesse accadendo. Le settimane si scioglievano in mesi, i mesi in anni, e gli anni in decenni, mentre il dotato Mosè rimaneva un pastore sotto rendimento. Una delle cose più difficili con cui lottiamo è «aspettare». Quasi ogni cristiano affronterà un lungo tempo di tribolazione e ci è detto di: …non pensate strano della prova di fuoco che è per provare voi, come se vi fosse cosa strana che vi accadesse –1 Pietro 4:12. Ma non dovremmo giudicare i mezzi di Dio dal nostro fiacco senso, perché nel frattempo lo meraviglioso operare dell’attesa ci prepara per…

La promozione di Dio

38, 39, … 40 anni. Vieni ora dunque, e io ti manderò da Faraone, affinché tu faccia uscire il mio popolo, i figli d’Israele, dall’Egitto –Esodo 3:10.

Forse a Dio piace il numero 40, ma molto più probabilmente fu il tempo che servì a far cadere Mosè nel luogo della rinuncia. La sua autostima era stata completamente spenta, e umilmente chiede: …Chi sono io, perché io vada da Faraone, e perché io faccia uscire i figli d’Israele dall’Egitto? –Esodo 3:11.

Mosè non era meno qualificato di quanto fosse quarant’anni prima, ma la sua presunzione era evaporata nel calore del sole del deserto. L’esperienza acquisita nei pascoli aspri con le pecore testarde lo aveva portato a comprendere che ciò sarebbe stato quasi un’impresa impossibile. Ma non esiste chiamata ordinata che sia emessa indipendentemente da…

La promessa di Dio

…Certo io sarò con te; e questa ti sarà per segno che io ti ho mandato: Quando avrai fatto uscire il popolo dall’Egitto, servirete Dio su questo monte –Esodo 3:12.

Non che Mosè avesse raggiunto la perfezione, poiché troviamo Mosè a irritare Dio nell’immediato capitolo successivo—E l’ira del Signore si accese contro Mosè… –Esodo 4:14. Poi di nuovo egli è oggetto diretto nel cammino della spada di Dio—E avvenne per la via nell’albergo, che il Signore lo incontrò e volle farlo morire –Esodo 4:24. Nonostante ciò, mentre il suo vaso è ancora di argilla, ha subito una cottura che lo ha preparato per il servizio del Signore, e per noi Dio non revoca le sue promesse al vento dei nostri capricci. Dunque, il grande IO SONO COLUI CHE SONO –vedi Esodo 3:14, ha posto sulle spalle umane l’immensa e eterna impresa di guidare il suo popolo. Ma questo incarico non deve essere eseguito senza…

La potenza di Dio

Qual è stata la vera raffinazione del tempo che Mosè trascorse nel deserto? Notiamo la sua pronta inclinazione a brandire la spada prima del suo arrivo, ma al suo uscire portava solo un bastone in mano. Con la spada aveva vinto un oppressore egiziano, ma con il bastone sconfisse le intere forze d’Egitto. Il bastone di Dio fece sgorgare acqua nel deserto. Fu il bastone di Dio che, quando elevato in alto da mani fragili, assicurò la vittoria su Amalek. Cos’è il bastone di Dio? Prima dei suoi giorni in Madian, a malapena ne conosceva l’esistenza. Quarant’anni dopo quasi non esiste scena senza di esso.

Il bastone è la potenza di Dio per la salvezza. È la sapienza di Dio, la verità di Dio, la testimonianza di Dio, ma più di tutte queste è la castigazione di Dio. Senza di esso, l’uomo non riceve né percepisce l’amore di Dio perché senza di esso l’uomo non è connesso a Dio. Perché il Signore corregge chi ama, e castiga ogni figlio che riceve. Se sopportate la correzione, Dio vi tratta come figli; poiché qual figlio è quello che il padre non corregge? Ma se siete senza correzione, della quale tutti sono partecipi, siete bastardi e non figli –Ebrei 12:6-8.

Quello stesso Mosè, che un tempo era disposto ad esercitare signoria (autorità gentile) sul popolo di Dio ora si trova a supplicare Dio e a trattenere la sua ira dall’anneggiarli. Le persone che accusarono Mosè di condurli fuori per farli morire e che a un certo punto erano pronte a lapidarlo sono ora al centro del suo cuore e della sua affezione, sebbene siano causa del suo fallimento nell’entrare nella terra promessa. Questo è l’amore di Cristo. Ma dove si apprende questo se non sotto il bastone di Dio, sul retro del deserto, nelle segrete egiziane, nelle caverne di Adulàm, nelle ristrettezze dell’Arabia, e nella silenziosa solitudine del retro fuoco dove Dio ha ordinato che molti dei suoi vadano finché imparino a …imparare da me; perché io sono mansueto e umile di cuore: e troverete riposo alle vostre anime –Matteo 11:29. Sicuramente è lì che Mosè assicurò il carattere noto allo studioso biblico come l’uomo più mansueto che abbia camminato sulla faccia della terra. Sicuramente non c’è luogo più opposto sulla terra per impararlo se non nella scuola della sofferenza.

E così qui dimoreremo anche noi, affinché …possiamo conoscerlo, e la potenza della sua risurrezione, e la comunione delle sue sofferenze, essendo fatti conformi alla sua morte –Filippesi 3:10.

Greetings to each one in the worthy name of Jesus Christ, our Saviour, and our Redeemer.

This magazine issue may seem to be arriving more quickly on the heels of the last one. True. We are continuing to tighten up our schedule as we work towards getting each quarterly issue out in a more timely manner. Our ultimate goal is to have them arrive in your mailboxes in the months of March, June, September, and December of each year. Pray for us as we continue moving towards that schedule.

From time to time, we receive feedback—suggestions, concerns, and encouragement. We value this feedback. It is filed away and used by the board as we continually evaluate ways to make our magazine better. One final thought on this matter… when we receive feedback of encouragement regarding a specific article, it is helpful for us, and it is encouraging for our authors as we pass that along to them. We welcome your ongoing feedback.

As previously mentioned, we are including several new categories in this issue. One on Church History that is being written by two young brothers from our church. And one on Hymn Histories being written by one of our board members, a middle-aged married man, who is also from our church.

In “Moses in Midian”, we take a walk in Moses’ footsteps during the mid-section of his life. He was uprooted from his comfortable lifestyle in Egypt as an adopted son of royalty and was then sent by God into the desert to learn some much-needed lessons in further preparation towards becoming God’s servant. As we take a look at the life of Jonah, we glean glimpses of “The God Who Will Not Let Go”. Often a struggling believer loses sight of the Truth of God because they believe the lie that no one cares, yet the truth of the matter is this—the God of the Bible doesn’t just drop us, or turn His back on us, the instant that we take a wrong turn or a misstep. Let’s allow this article to help us to become rooted and grounded in the biblical Truth of Abba Father—a Father who cares for His children. We also have the second article in a continuing series on discipleship, as well as an article written by a middle-aged, spiritually-mature sister who shares her encouragement for sisters to evaluate what God thinks of their attire.

Church History and Should A Christian Vote

Finally, let’s consider the two short articles on church history. One of our goals for this issue is burdened with the awareness that the country in which we live (the U.S.) is approaching mid-term elections in November of this year and that there will be a strong push for many conservative Anabaptists to become involved in the voting process to ensure a proper outcome for the good of their perceived cause or goals.

In the natural world our “old man” has the tendency to think that we must “do something” if we expect things to go in a “right” direction. The spiritual Truth is this: The king’s heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will –Proverbs 21:1. If we think that, as believers, we will have a part in electing the “right” person in an election if we personally vote, let’s stop to consider what God Himself told Nebuchadnezzar. …That the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will –Daniel 4:31-32.

Throughout the history of the Anabaptist people there have been varied opinions on this matter, however, it is our wish to lift up the perspective that Jesus said …My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight … but now is my kingdom not from hence –John 18:36. When we understand and develop a personal world view that is founded on the two-kingdom principle, we realize that we must function as …strangers and pilgrims on the earth. [While we] …declare plainly that [we] seek a country …a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called [our] God: for he hath prepared for [us] a city –Hebrews 11:13-16. In all things involving political involvement, it is our encouragement that New Testament believers should obey the command to …come out from among them, and be ye separate… –2 Corinthians 6:17.

Let’s always cultivate a right attitude in our hearts so that our talk and actions reflect God’s view on the matter when He through the Apostle Paul tells us to: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God … For he is the minister of God to thee… –Romans 13:1-4.

It is in consideration of these thoughts that we wrote the two articles detailing very different times in the history of the church and what it was like for Christians to relate to the government of their day. Let us seriously ponder whether we can do more good by getting involved in politics, especially in the voting process. Or whether God wants us to pray for our elected officials, to view them as His servants, and to speak about them with respect. Ultimately, we must trust God to bring about His will for the winding down of the “clock of time” as time speeds onward towards the end of time. God will do this through hardening the hearts of ungodly men in positions of power, just like Pharaoh of old, to accomplish His sovereign will for the world.

So, what is the solution when we struggle within our hearts about the direction of our country and its growing instability or when we experience so much pressure from our peers or the society around us to get involved to make a difference? The Apostle Paul gives us very clear direction when he says, I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. 1 Timothy 2:1-2. The Christian’s secret power of influence lies in the power of prayer that is produced in the privacy of his or her closet. However, for this prayer to have power it must be produced out of a heart of faith—And Jesus said unto them … verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20. Let us always remember that …The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16.

Until the next time, may God be with each one and grant you grace and peace as you walk faithfully according to His Word. Let us pray for each other as we go through the trying times in our world today.

हमारे उद्धारकर्ता और हमारे मुक्तिदाता, प्रभु यीशु मसीह के योग्य नाम में प्रत्येक को अभिवादन।

यह पत्रिका अंक पिछले अंक की तुलना में अधिक शीघ्रता से दिखाई दे रहा होगा। सही कहा। हम प्रत्येक त्रैमासिक अंक को अधिक समय पर प्रकाशित करने की दिशा में काम करते हुए अपनी समय-सारिणी को लगातार कस रहे हैं। हमारा अंतिम लक्ष्य यह है कि ये अंक प्रत्येक वर्ष मार्च, जून, सितंबर और दिसंबर के महीनों में आपके मेलबॉक्स में पहुँचें। कृपया हमारे लिए प्रार्थना कीजिए क्योंकि हम उस समय-सारिणी की ओर बढ़ रहे हैं।

समय-समय पर हमें प्रतिक्रिया प्राप्त होती है—सुझाव, चिंताएँ, और प्रोत्साहन। हम इन प्रतिक्रियों को महत्व देते हैं। इन्हें फाइल किया जाता है और हमारे बोर्ड द्वारा हमारी पत्रिका को बेहतर बनाने के तरीकों का मूल्यांकन करते समय उपयोग किया जाता है। इस विषय पर एक अंतिम विचार… जब हमें किसी विशेष लेख के संबंध में प्रोत्साहन वाली प्रतिक्रिया मिलती है, तो यह हमारे लिए सहायक होता है, और इसे हम अपने लेखकों तक पहुँचाते हुए उन्हें प्रोत्साहित करते हैं। हम आपकी सतत प्रतिक्रिया का स्वागत करते हैं।

जैसा कि पहले उल्लेख किया गया है, हम इस अंक में कई नए वर्ग शामिल कर रहे हैं। एक चर्च इतिहास पर है जिसे हमारी चर्च के दो युवा भाइयों द्वारा लिखा जा रहा है। और एक भजन इतिहास पर है जिसे हमारे बोर्ड के एक सदस्य, एक मध्य-आयु के विवाहितชาย, जो हमारे चर्च से भी हैं, द्वारा लिखा जा रहा है।

“मिडियन में मूसा” में, हम मूसा के जीवन के मध्य भाग में उसके पदचिन्हों पर चलते हैं। उन्हें मिस्र में राजसी दत्तक पुत्र के आरामदायक जीवन से उखाड़ा गया और फिर परमेश्वर द्वारा रेगिस्तान भेजा गया ताकि वे परमेश्वर के सेवक बनने की आगे की तैयारी में कुछ बहुत आवश्यक पाठ सीख सकें। जब हम योना के जीवन को देखते हैं, तो हम “उस परमेश्वर” की झलकियाँ पाते हैं जो पकड़ना नहीं छोड़ेगा। अक्सर एक संघर्ष कर रहा विश्वासी परमेश्वर की सत्यता से दूर हो जाता है क्योंकि वह उस झूठ को मान लेता है कि कोई परवाह नहीं करता, परन्तु सच्चाई यह है—बाइबिल का परमेश्वर हमें बस छोड़कर नहीं चला जाता, न ही हम एक गलत मोड़ या गलती करते ही वह हमारी पीठ घुमा लेता है। आइए यह लेख हमें अब्बा पिता की बाइबिलीय सत्यता में जड़ और आधार पाने में मदद करे—एक ऐसा पिता जो अपने बच्चों की परवाह करता है। हमारे पास शिष्यत्व पर चल रही शृंखला का दूसरा लेख भी है, साथ ही एक मध्य-आयु, आध्यात्मिक रूप से परिपक्व बहन द्वारा लिखा एक लेख है जो बहनों को प्रोत्साहित करती है कि वे अपने वस्त्र पर परमेश्वर का क्या विचार है, इसका मूल्यांकन करें।

चर्च इतिहास और क्या एक ईसाई को वोट देना चाहिए

अंत में, आइए चर्च इतिहास पर दो संक्षिप्त लेखों पर विचार करें। इस अंक के लिए हमारे उद्देश्यों में से एक यह भी है कि जिस देश में हम रहते हैं (यू.एस.) वहां इस वर्ष नवंबर में मध्यावधि चुनाव आने वाले हैं और कई रूढ़िवादी अनाबप्तिस्टों के लिए मतदान प्रक्रिया में शामिल होने का एक मजबूत दबाव होगा ताकि वे अपने देखे हुए कारणों या लक्ष्यों के लिए एक उपयुक्त परिणाम सुनिश्चित कर सकें।

प्राकृतिक संसार में हमारा “पुराना मनुष्य” यह सोचने की प्रवृत्ति रखता है कि यदि हम चाहते हैं कि चीजें “सही” दिशा में जाएँ तो हमें “कुछ करना” चाहिए। आध्यात्मिक सत्य यह है: राजा का हृदय यहोवा के हाथ में रहता है; वह उसे जैसे नदियों के बहने के समान जहाँ मन करे मोड़ देता है। –Proverbs 21:1. यदि हम सोचते हैं कि, विश्वासी होने के नाते, यदि हम व्यक्तिगत रूप से मतदान करें तो हम किसी चुनाव में “सही” व्यक्ति को चुनने में भूमिका निभाएंगे, तो आईए हम यह विचार करें कि परमेश्वर ने नेबूचादनेज़र को क्या कहा था। …परमोच्च मनुष्यों के राज्य में राज्य करता है, और जिसको चाहे उसे देता है –Daniel 4:31-32.

अनाबप्तिस्ट लोगों के इतिहास में इस मुद्दे पर विभिन्न मत रहे हैं, तथापि, हमारी इच्छा यह दृष्टि उठाने की है कि यीशु ने कहा …मेरा राज्य इस संसार का नहीं है; यदि मेरा राज्य इस संसार का होता, तो मेरे दास लड़ते; पर अब मेरा राज्य यहाँ से नहीं है। –John 18:36. जब हम उस व्यक्तिगत विश्वदृष्टि को समझते और विकसित करते हैं जो दो-राज्य सिद्धांत पर आधारित है, तो हम समझते हैं कि हमें …धरती पर परदेशी और आतिथ्यकारी (यात्री) होने चाहिए। [जबकि हम] …खुलकर घोषणा करते हैं कि हम एक देश की खोज कर रहे हैं …एक बेहतर देश, अर्थात् स्वर्गीय; इसलिए परमेश्वर को हमारे परमेश्वर कहा जाना लज्जास्पद न था: क्योंकि उसने हमारे लिए एक नगर तैयार किया है। –Hebrews 11:13-16. राजनीतिक भागीदारी से संबंधित सभी मामलों में, हमारा प्रोत्साहन यह है कि नए नियम के विश्वासी उस आज्ञा का पालन करें कि …उनके मध्य से बहिष्कृत हो जाओ, और पृथक हो जाओ… –2 Corinthians 6:17.

आइए हम हमेशा अपने हृदय में एक यथोचित दृष्टिकोण पालें ताकि हमारी बात और कार्य परमेश्वर के इस विषय पर दृष्टि को परिलक्षित करें जब वह प्रेरित पौलुस के माध्यम से हमें बताता है: सब मनुष्य ऊँचे अधिकारों के अधीन हों; क्योंकि कोई अधिकार परमेश्वर से न होकर नहीं, और जो अधिकार हैं वे परमेश्वर द्वारा स्थापित किए गए हैं… क्योंकि वह तुम्हारे लिए परमेश्वर का सेवक है… –Romans 13:1-4.

इन विचारों के परिप्रेक्ष्य में ही हमने दो ऐसे लेख लिखे हैं जो चर्च के इतिहास में बहुत अलग समयों का विवरण देते हैं और यह कि उस समय के ईसाइयों के लिए अपने दिन के सरकार से संबंधित होना कैसा था। आइए गंभीरता से विचार करें कि क्या राजनीति में, विशेषकर मतदान प्रक्रिया में शामिल होकर, हम अधिक भला कर सकते हैं। या क्या परमेश्वर चाहता है कि हम अपने निर्वाचित अधिकारियों के लिए प्रार्थना करें, उन्हें उसके सेवकों के रूप में देखें, और उनके बारे में सम्मानपूर्वक बोलें। अन्ततः, हमें परमेश्वर पर भरोसा रखना चाहिए कि जैसे-जैसे समय अंत की ओर बढ़ रहा है और 'समय की घड़ी' घटती जा रही है, वह अपनी इच्छा पूरी करेगा। परमेश्वर यह करेगा जब वह सत्ता में असभ्य पुरुषों के हृदयों को कठोर कर देगा, बिलकुल वैसे जैसे पुराने फ़िरौन के साथ हुआ था, ताकि वह इस जगत के लिए अपनी सार्वभौमिक इच्छा पूरी कर सके।

तो, क्या समाधान है जब हम अपने हृदय में हमारे देश की दिशा और उसकी बढ़ती अस्थिरता के बारे में संघर्ष करते हैं या जब हमें अपने साथियों या आस-पास के समाज से इतना दबाव महसूस होता है कि हमें शामिल होना चाहिए ताकि फर्क पड़े? प्रेरित पौलुस हमें बहुत स्पष्ट दिशा देता है जब वह कहता है, इसलिए मैं उत्साहपूर्वक उपदेश करता हूँ कि सब प्रकार की विनतीयें, प्रार्थनाएँ, मध्यस्थताएँ और धन्यवाद देना सब मनुष्यों के लिए की जाएँ; विशेषकर राजाओं और सभी अधिकार रखने वालों के लिए; ताकि हम सब भक्ति और सज्जनता में शांत और धैर्यपूर्ण जीवन बिताएँ। 1 Timothy 2:1-2. ईसाई का गुप्त प्रभावशाली बल उसके कपाट के भीतर पैदा होने वाली प्रार्थना की शक्ति में निहित है। हालांकि, इस प्रार्थना में शक्ति होने के लिए यह विश्वास के हृदय से उत्पन्न होनी चाहिए—और यीशु ने उनसे कहा… मैं तुमसे सच्च कहा देता हूँ, यदि तुम्हारे पास सरसों के दाने के समान श्रद्धा हो, तो तुम इस पहाड़ से कहोगे, यहाँ से वहां हट जा; और वह हट जाएगा; और तुम्हारे लिए कुछ भी असंभव न होगा। –Matthew 17:20. आइए हम सदैव यह याद रखें कि धर्मी मनुष्य की प्रभावशाली उत्तेजित प्रार्थना बहुत कुछ कर सकती है। –James 5:16.

अगली बार तक, परमेश्वर प्रत्येक के साथ रहें और आपको उस अनुग्रह और शांति से परिपूर्ण करें जैसा कि आप उसकी वचन के अनुसार विश्वासनिष्ठ रूप से चलते हैं। आइए आज की दुनिया के कठिन समयों से गुजरते हुए एक-दूसरे के लिए प्रार्थना करें।

Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created –Revelation 4:11.

This hymn, often called the “National Anthem of Christendom,” is perhaps one of the greatest of hymns of all time. It was written by Edward Perronet, first appearing in the November 1779 issue of Gospel Magazine. It was edited by Augustus Toplady, who is also the author of another well-known hymn, “Rock of Ages”. The text of this hymn, All Hail the Power of Jesus Name, has been translated into almost every language where Christianity is known. Wherever it is sung, it communicates to the spiritual needs of human hearts. One writer has said, “So long as there are Christians on earth, it will continue to be sung; and after that, in heaven.”

Edward Perronet was born at Sundridge, Kent, England, in 1726. He was a descendant of a distinguished French Huguenot family who had fled to Switzerland and later to England because of the religious persecution in France. Edward’s father, a pastor in the State Church of England, was strongly sympathetic with the evangelical movement spearheaded by the Wesleys and George Whitefield. Edward, too, like his father, became a minister in the Anglican Church but was always critical of its ways. Once he wrote, “I was born and I am likely to die in the tottering communion of the Church of England, but I despise her nonsense.” Soon, however, he broke from the Church and threw himself strenuously into the evangelistic endeavors of the Wesleys during the 1740s and 1750s.

Charles Wesley writes of Edward Perronet’s boldness in preaching. At one time he and Perronet were beset in a house by a mob of rough revilers, whom Perronet opposed courageously, while they abused him and threw dirt on him. It was during this time that the Wesleys and their followers suffered much persecution and even violence from those who disagreed with their ministry. Concerning these experiences, Wesley made the following notation in his diary: “From Rockdale we went to Bolton, and soon found that the Rockdale lions were lambs in comparison with those of Bolton.” Edward Perronet was thrown down and rolled in mud and mire. Stones were hurled and windows broken.

Another interesting account is given regarding the relationship between the Wesleys and Perronet. John Wesley wanted to hear Perronet preach, and he, being 18 years younger than John had always refused to preach in the older churchman’s presence. So, one day Wesley seeing Edward in the congregation announced that he would preach at the next service. Desiring to avoid a public conflict with Wesley, Perronet mounted the pulpit the next morning, but quickly explained that he had never consented to preach. “However,” he added, “I shall deliver the greatest sermon that has ever been preached on earth.” He then read the Sermon on the Mount and sat down without comment.

After eight years of co-operation with the Wesleys, Perronet’s strong-mindedness and free spirit caused a division between them, as he disagreed with some of their regulations. They continued, however, to esteem and love each other.

The last years of Perronet were spent at Canterbury, where he was pastor of an independent church, and where he died in 1792, at the age of sixty-six. His last words have also become a classic: “Glory to God in the height of His divinity! Glory to God in the depth of His humanity! Glory to God in His all-sufficiency! Into His hands I commend my spirit.”

Though Perronet wrote many other hymns and forms of poetry, none of them, have attained fame except the immortal “All Hail the Power of Jesus Name.” The success of this text has, no doubt, been furthered by three fine tunes. “Coronation,” composed by Oliver Holden, a Massachusetts carpenter, self-taught musician, and respected singing-school teacher, is most widely used in America. “Miles Lane” composed by William Shrubsole, Perronet’s personal friend, is the most popular in Great Britain. While the festive “Diadem” tune, composed in 1838 for this text by James Ellor, an English layman, is frequently used as a choir number. This hymn was originally written having the title, “On the Resurrection,” and there were eight stanzas, as follows:

All hail the power of Jesus’ name,
Let angels prostrate fall
Bring forth the royal diadem,
To crown Him Lord of all!

Let high born seraphs tune the lyre,
And, as they tune it, fall
Before His face who tunes their choir,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye morning stars of light,
Who fixed this floating ball,
Now hail the Strength of Israel’s might,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God,
Who from His altar call;
Extol the stem of Jesse’s rod,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Ye seed of Israel’s chosen race,
Ye ransomed of the fall,
Hail Him who saves you by His grace
And crown Him Lord of all!

Hail Him, ye heirs of David’s line,
Whom David Lord did call.
The God incarnate, Man divine,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Sinners, whose love can ne’er forget
The wormwood and the gall,
Go spread your trophies at His feet,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Let every tribe and every tongue
That bound creation’s call
Now shout in universal song,
The crowned Lord of all!

As it now stands in our hymnbooks, the hymn is shortened and changed, and one stanza has been added by the famous hymn collector, Rev. John Rippon, in 1787.

Oh, that with yonder sacred throng
We at His feet may fall;
We’ll join the everlasting song,
And crown Him Lord of all.

As we wrap up this amazing story of the life of Edward Perronet and the others who have had their part in bringing this immortal hymn to us, let’s take a look in closing at the effect this hymn has had on heathens who knew nothing about Jesus. The most famous story connected with Perronet’s great hymn is told of the missionary to India, Rev. E.P. Scott. One day he saw on the street a man of so strange an appearance that he inquired about him and learned that he belonged to a wild mountain tribe among whom Christ had never been preached. Mr. Scott prayed over the matter and decided to visit that tribe. As soon as he reached their mountain home, he fell in among a savage band of murderous tribesmen who were on a war expedition, and who were closing in on him with their spears. They seized him and pointed their spears at his heart. At once the missionary drew out the violin that he always carried with him and began to play and sing in the native language, “All hail the power of Jesus’ name!” He closed his eyes, expecting death at any minute. When he reached the fourth stanza, and nothing had happened, he opened his eyes, and was amazed to see that the spears had fallen from the hands of the savages, and big tears were in their eyes! They invited Mr. Scott to their homes, and he spent the remaining years of his life preaching and ministering God’s love and redemption to these people. God in His providence used a simple hymn as a means of introducing the gospel to a group of needy pagans.
