Tu es digne, ô Seigneur, de recevoir la gloire, l'honneur et la puissance: car tu as créé toutes choses, et c'est pour ton plaisir qu'elles existent et ont été créées –Apocalypse 4:11.

Cet hymne, souvent appelé «l'hymne national du christianisme», est peut-être l'un des plus grands hymnes de tous les temps. Il a été écrit par Edward Perronet et est paru pour la première fois dans le numéro de novembre 1779 du Gospel Magazine. Il a été édité par Augustus Toplady, qui est aussi l'auteur d'un autre hymne bien connu, «Rock of Ages». Le texte de cet hymne, «Salut au pouvoir du nom de Jésus» (All Hail the Power of Jesus' Name), a été traduit dans presque toutes les langues où le christianisme est connu. Partout où il est chanté, il répond aux besoins spirituels des cœurs humains. Un écrivain a dit : «Tant qu'il y aura des chrétiens sur terre, il continuera d'être chanté; et ensuite, au ciel.»

Edward Perronet est né à Sundridge, dans le Kent, en Angleterre, en 1726. Il descendait d'une illustre famille huguenote française qui avait fui en Suisse puis en Angleterre à cause des persécutions religieuses en France. Le père d'Edward, pasteur dans l'Église d'Angleterre, était fortement sympathisant du mouvement évangélique mené par les frères Wesley et George Whitefield. Edward, lui aussi, comme son père, devint ministre dans l'Église anglicane mais fut toujours critique à l'égard de ses façons. Il écrivit une fois : «Je suis né et je suis susceptible de mourir dans la communion vacillante de l'Église d'Angleterre, mais je méprise ses absurdités.» Bientôt cependant, il rompit avec l'Église et se lança avec énergie dans les œuvres évangéliques des Wesley durant les années 1740 et 1750.

Charles Wesley écrit sur l'audace d'Edward Perronet dans la prédication. À une époque, lui et Perronet furent assiégés dans une maison par une foule de grossiers vociférateurs, que Perronet affronta courageusement, tandis qu'ils l'insultaient et lui jetaient de la terre. C'est à cette période que les Wesley et leurs partisans subirent beaucoup de persécution et même de la violence de la part de ceux qui désapprouvaient leur ministère. Concernant ces expériences, Wesley nota dans son journal : «De Rockdale nous sommes allés à Bolton, et nous avons bientôt trouvé que les lions de Rockdale étaient des agneaux comparés à ceux de Bolton.» Edward Perronet fut jeté à terre et roulé dans la boue et la fange. Des pierres furent lancées et des fenêtres brisées.

Un autre récit intéressant est donné concernant la relation entre les Wesley et Perronet. John Wesley désirait entendre Perronet prêcher, et lui, étant de dix-huit ans plus jeune que John, avait toujours refusé de prêcher en présence du vieux pasteur. Ainsi, un jour, Wesley voyant Edward dans la congrégation annonça qu'il prêcherait au service suivant. Désirant éviter un conflit public avec Wesley, Perronet monta en chaire le lendemain matin, mais expliqua rapidement qu'il n'avait jamais consenti à prêcher. «Cependant,» ajouta-t-il, «je livrerai le plus grand sermon qui ait jamais été prêché sur la terre.» Il lut alors le Sermon sur la montagne et s'assit sans commentaire.

Après huit années de coopération avec les Wesley, l'entêtement et l'esprit libre de Perronet provoquèrent une division entre eux, car il était en désaccord avec certaines de leurs règlements. Ils continuèrent néanmoins à s'estimer et à s'aimer.

Les dernières années de Perronet se passèrent à Canterbury, où il fut pasteur d'une église indépendante, et où il mourut en 1792, à l'âge de soixante-six ans. Ses dernières paroles sont également devenues un classique : «Gloire à Dieu dans la hauteur de Sa divinité! Gloire à Dieu dans la profondeur de Son humanité! Gloire à Dieu dans Sa suffisance totale! Entre Ses mains je recommande mon esprit.»

Bien que Perronet ait écrit de nombreux autres hymnes et poèmes, aucun d'eux n'a acquis de renommée excepté l'immortel «All Hail the Power of Jesus' Name». Le succès de ce texte a sans doute été favorisé par trois beaux airs. «Coronation», composé par Oliver Holden, un charpentier du Massachusetts, musicien autodidacte et respecté professeur d'école de chant, est le plus largement utilisé en Amérique. «Miles Lane», composé par William Shrubsole, ami personnel de Perronet, est le plus populaire en Grande-Bretagne. Tandis que l'air festif «Diadem», composé en 1838 pour ce texte par James Ellor, un laïc anglais, est fréquemment utilisé comme pièce de chœur. Cet hymne a été à l'origine écrit sous le titre «On the Resurrection», et il y avait huit strophes, comme suit :

Salut au pouvoir du nom de Jésus,
Que les anges se prosternent et tombent!
Apportez la diadème royal,
Pour le couronner Seigneur de tout!

Que les séraphins nés en haut accordent la lyre,
Et, tandis qu'ils l'accordent, s'inclinent,
Devant Sa face qui règle leur chœur,
Et le couronner Seigneur de tout!

Couronnez-Le, ô étoiles matinales de lumière,
Qui avez fixé cette boule flottante,
Saluez maintenant la Force de la puissance d'Israël,
Et couronnez-Le Seigneur de tout!

Couronnez-Le, ô martyrs de votre Dieu,
Qui l'appelez de son autel;
Exaltez la tige du bâton de Jessé,
Et couronnez-Le Seigneur de tout!

Vous, semence de la race choisie d'Israël,
Vous, rachetés de la chute,
Saluez Celui qui vous sauve par Sa grâce
Et couronnez-Le Seigneur de tout!

Saluez-Le, héritiers de la lignée de David,
Que David appelait Seigneur.
Le Dieu incarné, l'Homme divin,
Et couronnez-Le Seigneur de tout!

Pécheurs, dont l'amour ne peut jamais oublier
L'absinthe et la bile,
Allez répandre vos trophées à Ses pieds,
Et couronnez-Le Seigneur de tout!

Que chaque tribu et chaque langue
Qui a lié l'appel de la création
Crie maintenant dans un chant universel,
Le Seigneur couronné de tout!

Tel qu'il figure maintenant dans nos recueils d'hymnes, l'hymne est abrégé et modifié, et une strophe a été ajoutée par le célèbre collecteur d'hymnes, le révérend John Rippon, en 1787.

Oh, que nous, avec cette sainte multitude là-bas,
Puissions tomber à Ses pieds;
Nous nous joindrons au chant éternel,
Et le couronnerons Seigneur de tout.

Alors que nous concluons cette histoire étonnante de la vie d'Edward Perronet et des autres qui ont contribué à nous transmettre cet hymne immortel, examinons enfin l'effet qu'a eu cet hymne sur des païens qui ne connaissaient rien de Jésus. L'histoire la plus célèbre liée au grand hymne de Perronet est racontée au sujet du missionnaire en Inde, le rév. E. P. Scott. Un jour il vit dans la rue un homme d'apparence si étrange qu'il s'enquit à son sujet et apprit qu'il appartenait à une tribu montagnarde sauvage parmi laquelle le Christ n'avait jamais été prêché. M. Scott pria sur la question et décida de visiter cette tribu. Dès qu'il atteignit leur demeure montagneuse, il tomba au milieu d'une bande sauvage de tribus meurtrières qui étaient en expédition de guerre, et qui l'entouraient avec leurs lances. Ils le saisirent et pointèrent leurs lances vers son cœur. Aussitôt le missionnaire sortit le violon qu'il portait toujours avec lui et se mit à jouer et chanter dans la langue native, «Salut au pouvoir du nom de Jésus!» Il ferma les yeux, s'attendant à la mort à tout instant. Lorsqu'il atteignit la quatrième strophe, et que rien ne se fut produit, il ouvrit les yeux, et fut étonné de voir que les lances étaient tombées des mains des sauvages, et de grosses larmes brillaient dans leurs yeux! Ils invitèrent M. Scott dans leurs foyers, et il passa les années restantes de sa vie à prêcher et à manifester l'amour et la rédemption de Dieu à ces peuples. Dieu, dans Sa providence, utilisa un simple hymne comme moyen d'introduire l'Évangile à un groupe de païens dans le besoin.

«Miles Lane» Tune -William Shrubsole, 1760-1806
«Diadem» Tune -James Elliot, 1838
«Let Us Crown Him» Tune -James McGranahan 1840-1907

Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created –Revelation 4:11.

This hymn, often called the “National Anthem of Christendom,” is perhaps one of the greatest of hymns of all time. It was written by Edward Perronet, first appearing in the November 1779 issue of Gospel Magazine. It was edited by Augustus Toplady, who is also the author of another well-known hymn, “Rock of Ages”. The text of this hymn, All Hail the Power of Jesus Name, has been translated into almost every language where Christianity is known. Wherever it is sung, it communicates to the spiritual needs of human hearts. One writer has said, “So long as there are Christians on earth, it will continue to be sung; and after that, in heaven.”

Edward Perronet was born at Sundridge, Kent, England, in 1726. He was a descendant of a distinguished French Huguenot family who had fled to Switzerland and later to England because of the religious persecution in France. Edward’s father, a pastor in the State Church of England, was strongly sympathetic with the evangelical movement spearheaded by the Wesleys and George Whitefield. Edward, too, like his father, became a minister in the Anglican Church but was always critical of its ways. Once he wrote, “I was born and I am likely to die in the tottering communion of the Church of England, but I despise her nonsense.” Soon, however, he broke from the Church and threw himself strenuously into the evangelistic endeavors of the Wesleys during the 1740s and 1750s.

Charles Wesley writes of Edward Perronet’s boldness in preaching. At one time he and Perronet were beset in a house by a mob of rough revilers, whom Perronet opposed courageously, while they abused him and threw dirt on him. It was during this time that the Wesleys and their followers suffered much persecution and even violence from those who disagreed with their ministry. Concerning these experiences, Wesley made the following notation in his diary: “From Rockdale we went to Bolton, and soon found that the Rockdale lions were lambs in comparison with those of Bolton.” Edward Perronet was thrown down and rolled in mud and mire. Stones were hurled and windows broken.

Another interesting account is given regarding the relationship between the Wesleys and Perronet. John Wesley wanted to hear Perronet preach, and he, being 18 years younger than John had always refused to preach in the older churchman’s presence. So, one day Wesley seeing Edward in the congregation announced that he would preach at the next service. Desiring to avoid a public conflict with Wesley, Perronet mounted the pulpit the next morning, but quickly explained that he had never consented to preach. “However,” he added, “I shall deliver the greatest sermon that has ever been preached on earth.” He then read the Sermon on the Mount and sat down without comment.

After eight years of co-operation with the Wesleys, Perronet’s strong-mindedness and free spirit caused a division between them, as he disagreed with some of their regulations. They continued, however, to esteem and love each other.

The last years of Perronet were spent at Canterbury, where he was pastor of an independent church, and where he died in 1792, at the age of sixty-six. His last words have also become a classic: “Glory to God in the height of His divinity! Glory to God in the depth of His humanity! Glory to God in His all-sufficiency! Into His hands I commend my spirit.”

Though Perronet wrote many other hymns and forms of poetry, none of them, have attained fame except the immortal “All Hail the Power of Jesus Name.” The success of this text has, no doubt, been furthered by three fine tunes. “Coronation,” composed by Oliver Holden, a Massachusetts carpenter, self-taught musician, and respected singing-school teacher, is most widely used in America. “Miles Lane” composed by William Shrubsole, Perronet’s personal friend, is the most popular in Great Britain. While the festive “Diadem” tune, composed in 1838 for this text by James Ellor, an English layman, is frequently used as a choir number. This hymn was originally written having the title, “On the Resurrection,” and there were eight stanzas, as follows:

All hail the power of Jesus’ name,
Let angels prostrate fall
Bring forth the royal diadem,
To crown Him Lord of all!

Let high born seraphs tune the lyre,
And, as they tune it, fall
Before His face who tunes their choir,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye morning stars of light,
Who fixed this floating ball,
Now hail the Strength of Israel’s might,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God,
Who from His altar call;
Extol the stem of Jesse’s rod,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Ye seed of Israel’s chosen race,
Ye ransomed of the fall,
Hail Him who saves you by His grace
And crown Him Lord of all!

Hail Him, ye heirs of David’s line,
Whom David Lord did call.
The God incarnate, Man divine,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Sinners, whose love can ne’er forget
The wormwood and the gall,
Go spread your trophies at His feet,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Let every tribe and every tongue
That bound creation’s call
Now shout in universal song,
The crowned Lord of all!

As it now stands in our hymnbooks, the hymn is shortened and changed, and one stanza has been added by the famous hymn collector, Rev. John Rippon, in 1787.

Oh, that with yonder sacred throng
We at His feet may fall;
We’ll join the everlasting song,
And crown Him Lord of all.

As we wrap up this amazing story of the life of Edward Perronet and the others who have had their part in bringing this immortal hymn to us, let’s take a look in closing at the effect this hymn has had on heathens who knew nothing about Jesus. The most famous story connected with Perronet’s great hymn is told of the missionary to India, Rev. E.P. Scott. One day he saw on the street a man of so strange an appearance that he inquired about him and learned that he belonged to a wild mountain tribe among whom Christ had never been preached. Mr. Scott prayed over the matter and decided to visit that tribe. As soon as he reached their mountain home, he fell in among a savage band of murderous tribesmen who were on a war expedition, and who were closing in on him with their spears. They seized him and pointed their spears at his heart. At once the missionary drew out the violin that he always carried with him and began to play and sing in the native language, “All hail the power of Jesus’ name!” He closed his eyes, expecting death at any minute. When he reached the fourth stanza, and nothing had happened, he opened his eyes, and was amazed to see that the spears had fallen from the hands of the savages, and big tears were in their eyes! They invited Mr. Scott to their homes, and he spent the remaining years of his life preaching and ministering God’s love and redemption to these people. God in His providence used a simple hymn as a means of introducing the gospel to a group of needy pagans.

Du er verdig, Herre, til å få ære, ære og makt; for du skapte alle ting, og ved din vilje er de og ble de skapt – Åpenbaringen 4:11.

Denne salmen, ofte kalt «Kristendommens nasjonalsang», er kanskje en av de største salmene gjennom tidene. Den ble skrevet av Edward Perronet og sto først i Gospel Magazine i november 1779. Den ble redigert av Augustus Toplady, som også er forfatteren av en annen velkjent salme, «Rock of Ages». Teksten til denne salmen, «Hyll kraften i Jesu navn», er blitt oversatt til nesten alle språk hvor kristendommen er kjent. Hvor enn den synges, treffer den menneskehjertets åndelige behov. En forfatter har sagt: «Så lenge det finnes kristne på jorden, vil den fortsette å bli sunget; og etter det, i himmelen.»

Edward Perronet ble født i Sundridge, Kent, England, i 1726. Han stammet fra en fremtredende fransk hugenottfamilie som hadde flyktet til Sveits og senere til England på grunn av den religiøse forfølgelsen i Frankrike. Edwards far, en prest i den engelske statskirken, hadde sterk sympati for den evangeliske bevegelsen ledet av Wesley-brødrene og George Whitefield. Edward ble, lik sin far, også prest i den anglikanske kirken, men var alltid kritisk til dens væremåte. En gang skrev han: «Jeg ble født og jeg kommer trolig til å dø i den vaklende kommunionen i den engelske kirke, men jeg forakter hennes tåpeligheter.» Snart brøt han imidlertid med kirken og engasjerte seg energisk i Wesley-brødrenes evangeliske arbeid på 1740- og 1750-tallet.

Charles Wesley skriver om Edward Perronets frimodighet i forkynnelsen. En gang ble han og Perronet beleiret i et hus av en mobb med grove skjennere, som Perronet møtte med mot mens de fornærmet ham og kastet jord på ham. Det var i denne tiden at Wesley-brødrene og deres tilhengere ble utsatt for mye forfølgelse og til og med vold fra dem som var uenige i deres tjeneste. Om disse erfaringene noterte Wesley i sin dagbok: «Fra Rockdale dro vi til Bolton, og snart fant vi at Rockdale-løvene var lammer sammenlignet med dem i Bolton.» Edward Perronet ble kastet ned og rullet i søle og gjørme. Steiner ble kastet og vinduer knust.

En annen interessant beretning gjelder forholdet mellom Wesley-brødrene og Perronet. John Wesley ønsket å høre Perronet forkynne, og Perronet, som var 18 år yngre enn John, hadde alltid nektet å forkynne i den eldre kirkemannens nærvær. Så en dag, da Wesley så Edward i menigheten, annonserte han at han ville preke ved neste samling. For å unngå en offentlig konflikt med Wesley gikk Perronet opp i prekestolen neste morgen, men forklarte raskt at han aldri hadde samtykket til å preke. «Likevel,» la han til, «vil jeg holde den største prekenen som noen gang er holdt på jorden.» Han leste så Bergprekenen og satte seg ned uten kommentar.

Etter åtte år med samarbeid med Wesley-brødrene førte Perronets stahet og frie ånd til en splittelse mellom dem, ettersom han var uenig i noen av deres regler. De fortsatte imidlertid å holde av hverandre og elske hverandre.

De siste årene av Perronets liv ble tilbrakt i Canterbury, hvor han var pastor for en uavhengig menighet, og hvor han døde i 1792, i en alder av sekstiseks år. Hans siste ord har også blitt klassiske: «Ære være Gud i høyden for Hans guddommelighet! Ære være Gud i dybden for Hans menneskelighet! Ære være Gud i Hans alt-tilstrekkelighet! I Hans hender overgir jeg min ånd.»

Selv om Perronet skrev mange andre salmer og diktformer, har ingen av dem oppnådd berømmelse bortsett fra den udødelige «All Hail the Power of Jesus Name». Tekstens suksess har utvilsomt blitt fremmet av tre gode melodier. «Coronation», komponert av Oliver Holden, en snekker fra Massachusetts, selvlært musiker og respektert sangskolelærer, er mest brukt i Amerika. «Miles Lane», komponert av William Shrubsole, Perronets personlige venn, er mest populær i Storbritannia. Mens den festlige «Diadem»-melodien, komponert i 1838 til denne teksten av James Ellor, en engelsk lekperson, ofte brukes som korstykke. Denne salmen ble opprinnelig skrevet med tittelen «On the Resurrection», og den hadde åtte vers, som følger:

Heil over Jesu navn i makt,
La engler kaste seg ned!
Framfør den kongelige krone prakt,
Og kroner Ham til Herre for alt!

La høye serafers strenger kling
Og når de klinger, fall
For Hans åsyn som dirigerer deres sang,
Og krone Ham til Herre for alt!

Kron Ham, dere morgenstjerner så klare,
Som fastla dette flytende klodeball,
Gni nå Israels styrkes navn og prise Ham fare,
Og krone Ham til Herre for alt!

Kron Ham, dere martyrer for Gud,
Som fra Hans alter kaller;
Forherlig Jesajas stamme, roden brud,
Og krone Ham til Herre for alt!

Dere sæd av Israels utvalgte ætt,
Dere som fra fallet er løst,
Hyl Ham som frelser ved sin nådes makt,
Og krone Ham til Herre for alt!

Hyl Ham, dere arvinger av Davids slekt,
Som David selv til Herre kalte.
Gud inkarnert, Menneske guddommelig vekt,
Og krone Ham til Herre for alt!

Synderes kjærlighet som aldri glemmer
Bitre sorgens, gallens kval,
Spre deres troféer ved Hans føtter frem,
Og krone Ham til Herre for alt!

La hvert stamme og hver tunge kalle
Som bundet skapelsens lov,
Nå juble i en universell salme alle,
Den kronede Herre for alt!

Som den nå står i våre salmebøker, er salmen forkortet og endret, og ett vers ble lagt til av den berømte salmesamleren, prest John Rippon, i 1787.

Å, at vi med den hellige skare der
Ved Hans føtter måtte falle;
Vi går med i den evige salmesvar,
Og krone Ham til Herre for alt.

Når vi avrunder denne bemerkelsesverdige beretningen om livet til Edward Perronet og de andre som har hatt sin del i å bringe denne udødelige salmen til oss, la oss til slutt se på hvilken virkning denne salmen har hatt på hedninger som ikke kjente til Jesus. Den mest berømte historien knyttet til Perronets store salme fortelles om misjonæren til India, Rev. E. P. Scott. En dag så han i gaten en mann med så merkelig utseende at han spurte om ham og fikk vite at han tilhørte en vill fjellstamme hvor Kristus aldri var blitt forkynt. Mr. Scott ba over saken og besluttet å besøke stammen. Så snart han nådde deres fjellhjem, falt han blant en vill bande av mordiske stammemenn som var på krigstokt, og som nærmet seg ham med spyd. De grep ham og pekte spyd mot hans hjerte. Med en gang tok misjonæren fram fiolinen han alltid bar med seg og begynte å spille og synge på morsmålet: «All hail the power of Jesus’ name!» Han lukket øynene, forventet å dø hvert øyeblikk. Da han nådde fjerde vers, og ingenting hadde skjedd, åpnet han øynene og ble forbauset over å se at spydene hadde falt fra de villmennenes hender, og store tårer fylte øynene deres! De inviterte Mr. Scott til hjemmene sine, og han tilbrakte de gjenværende årene av sitt liv med å forkynne og tjene Guds kjærlighet og forløsning for disse menneskene. Gud brukte i sin forsyn en enkel salme som et middel til å introdusere evangeliet for en gruppe trengende hedninger.

Greetings to each one in the worthy name of Jesus Christ, our Saviour, and our Redeemer.

This magazine issue may seem to be arriving more quickly on the heels of the last one. True. We are continuing to tighten up our schedule as we work towards getting each quarterly issue out in a more timely manner. Our ultimate goal is to have them arrive in your mailboxes in the months of March, June, September, and December of each year. Pray for us as we continue moving towards that schedule.

From time to time, we receive feedback—suggestions, concerns, and encouragement. We value this feedback. It is filed away and used by the board as we continually evaluate ways to make our magazine better. One final thought on this matter… when we receive feedback of encouragement regarding a specific article, it is helpful for us, and it is encouraging for our authors as we pass that along to them. We welcome your ongoing feedback.

As previously mentioned, we are including several new categories in this issue. One on Church History that is being written by two young brothers from our church. And one on Hymn Histories being written by one of our board members, a middle-aged married man, who is also from our church.

In “Moses in Midian”, we take a walk in Moses’ footsteps during the mid-section of his life. He was uprooted from his comfortable lifestyle in Egypt as an adopted son of royalty and was then sent by God into the desert to learn some much-needed lessons in further preparation towards becoming God’s servant. As we take a look at the life of Jonah, we glean glimpses of “The God Who Will Not Let Go”. Often a struggling believer loses sight of the Truth of God because they believe the lie that no one cares, yet the truth of the matter is this—the God of the Bible doesn’t just drop us, or turn His back on us, the instant that we take a wrong turn or a misstep. Let’s allow this article to help us to become rooted and grounded in the biblical Truth of Abba Father—a Father who cares for His children. We also have the second article in a continuing series on discipleship, as well as an article written by a middle-aged, spiritually-mature sister who shares her encouragement for sisters to evaluate what God thinks of their attire.

Church History and Should A Christian Vote

Finally, let’s consider the two short articles on church history. One of our goals for this issue is burdened with the awareness that the country in which we live (the U.S.) is approaching mid-term elections in November of this year and that there will be a strong push for many conservative Anabaptists to become involved in the voting process to ensure a proper outcome for the good of their perceived cause or goals.

In the natural world our “old man” has the tendency to think that we must “do something” if we expect things to go in a “right” direction. The spiritual Truth is this: The king’s heart is in the hand of the LORD, as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will –Proverbs 21:1. If we think that, as believers, we will have a part in electing the “right” person in an election if we personally vote, let’s stop to consider what God Himself told Nebuchadnezzar. …That the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will –Daniel 4:31-32.

Throughout the history of the Anabaptist people there have been varied opinions on this matter, however, it is our wish to lift up the perspective that Jesus said …My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight … but now is my kingdom not from hence –John 18:36. When we understand and develop a personal world view that is founded on the two-kingdom principle, we realize that we must function as …strangers and pilgrims on the earth. [While we] …declare plainly that [we] seek a country …a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called [our] God: for he hath prepared for [us] a city –Hebrews 11:13-16. In all things involving political involvement, it is our encouragement that New Testament believers should obey the command to …come out from among them, and be ye separate… –2 Corinthians 6:17.

Let’s always cultivate a right attitude in our hearts so that our talk and actions reflect God’s view on the matter when He through the Apostle Paul tells us to: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God … For he is the minister of God to thee… –Romans 13:1-4.

It is in consideration of these thoughts that we wrote the two articles detailing very different times in the history of the church and what it was like for Christians to relate to the government of their day. Let us seriously ponder whether we can do more good by getting involved in politics, especially in the voting process. Or whether God wants us to pray for our elected officials, to view them as His servants, and to speak about them with respect. Ultimately, we must trust God to bring about His will for the winding down of the “clock of time” as time speeds onward towards the end of time. God will do this through hardening the hearts of ungodly men in positions of power, just like Pharaoh of old, to accomplish His sovereign will for the world.

So, what is the solution when we struggle within our hearts about the direction of our country and its growing instability or when we experience so much pressure from our peers or the society around us to get involved to make a difference? The Apostle Paul gives us very clear direction when he says, I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. 1 Timothy 2:1-2. The Christian’s secret power of influence lies in the power of prayer that is produced in the privacy of his or her closet. However, for this prayer to have power it must be produced out of a heart of faith—And Jesus said unto them … verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20. Let us always remember that …The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16.

Until the next time, may God be with each one and grant you grace and peace as you walk faithfully according to His Word. Let us pray for each other as we go through the trying times in our world today.

Saludos a cada uno en el digno nombre de Jesucristo, nuestro Salvador y nuestro Redentor.

Esta edición de la revista puede parecer que llega más rápidamente tras la anterior. Es cierto. Seguimos ajustando nuestro calendario mientras trabajamos para publicar cada número trimestral de manera más oportuna. Nuestra meta final es que lleguen a sus buzones en los meses de marzo, junio, septiembre y diciembre de cada año. Oren por nosotros mientras seguimos avanzando hacia ese calendario.

De vez en cuando recibimos comentarios: sugerencias, inquietudes y estímulos. Valoramos estos comentarios. Se archivan y el consejo los utiliza mientras evaluamos continuamente maneras de mejorar la revista. Un último pensamiento sobre este asunto… cuando recibimos comentarios de ánimo respecto a un artículo específico, nos resulta útil y también es alentador para nuestros autores cuando se los transmitimos. Apreciamos sus comentarios continuos.

Como se mencionó anteriormente, estamos incluyendo varias categorías nuevas en este número. Una sobre Historia de la Iglesia que está siendo escrita por dos jóvenes hermanos de nuestra iglesia. Y otra sobre Historias de Himnos escrita por uno de los miembros de nuestro consejo, un hombre casado de mediana edad, que también es de nuestra iglesia.

En «Moisés en Madián», caminamos tras las huellas de Moisés durante la sección media de su vida. Fue arrancado de su estilo de vida cómodo en Egipto como hijo adoptivo de la realeza y luego enviado por Dios al desierto para aprender unas lecciones muy necesarias en preparación adicional para llegar a ser siervo de Dios. Al contemplar la vida de Jonás, vislumbramos a “El Dios que no suelta”. Con frecuencia un creyente en lucha pierde de vista la Verdad de Dios porque cree la mentira de que a nadie le importa; sin embargo, la verdad es esta: el Dios de la Biblia no nos abandona ni nos da la espalda en el instante en que tomamos un rumbo equivocado o damos un paso en falso. Permitamos que este artículo nos ayude a enraizarnos y afirmarnos en la Verdad bíblica del Abba Padre: un Padre que cuida de sus hijos. También tenemos el segundo artículo de una serie continua sobre el discipulado, así como un artículo escrito por una hermana de mediana edad y madura espiritualmente, que comparte su estímulo para que las hermanas evalúen lo que Dios piensa sobre su vestimenta.

Historia de la Iglesia y ¿Debería un cristiano votar?

Finalmente, consideremos los dos artículos breves sobre historia de la iglesia. Una de nuestras metas para este número está cargada con la conciencia de que el país en el que vivimos (EE. UU.) se aproxima a las elecciones de medio término en noviembre de este año y que habrá un fuerte impulso para que muchos anabaptistas conservadores se involucren en el proceso de votación para asegurar un resultado apropiado para el bien de su causa o de sus metas percibidas.

En el mundo natural nuestro “hombre viejo” tiene la tendencia a pensar que debemos “hacer algo” si esperamos que las cosas vayan en la dirección “correcta”. La verdad espiritual es esta: El corazón del rey está en la mano del SEÑOR, como los torrentes de las aguas; él lo inclina a donde quiere —Proverbios 21:1. Si pensamos que, como creyentes, tendremos parte en elegir a la persona “correcta” en una elección si votamos personalmente, detengámonos a considerar lo que Dios mismo le dijo a Nabucodonosor. …Que el Altísimo reina en el reino de los hombres, y lo da a quien él quiere —Daniel 4:31-32.

A lo largo de la historia del pueblo anabaptista ha habido opiniones variadas sobre este asunto; sin embargo, deseamos presentar la perspectiva de que Jesús dijo …Mi reino no es de este mundo; si mi reino fuera de este mundo, mis siervos pelearían… pero ahora mi reino no es de aquí —Juan 18:36. Cuando entendemos y desarrollamos una cosmovisión personal fundada en el principio de los dos reinos, nos damos cuenta de que debemos comportarnos como …extranjeros y peregrinos en la tierra. [Mientras] …declaramos públicamente que buscamos una patria… una mejor patria, es decir, celestial; por lo cual Dios no se avergüenza de ser llamado nuestro Dios: porque nos ha preparado una ciudad —Hebreos 11:13-16. En todo lo relacionado con la participación política, nuestro aliento es que los creyentes del Nuevo Testamento obedezcan el mandato de …salid de entre ellos, y apartaos… —2 Corintios 6:17.

Siempre cultivemos una actitud correcta en nuestros corazones para que nuestras palabras y acciones reflejen la perspectiva de Dios sobre el asunto cuando Él, por medio del apóstol Pablo, nos dice: Sométase toda persona a las autoridades superiores; porque no hay autoridad sino de parte de Dios, y las que hay, por Dios han sido establecidas… Porque el magistrado no es temor para las buenas obras, sino para las malas. ¿Quieres, pues, no temer la autoridad? Haz lo bueno, y tendrás alabanza de ella; porque es ministro de Dios para tu bien… —Romanos 13:1-4.

Es en consideración de estos pensamientos que escribimos los dos artículos que detallan épocas muy diferentes en la historia de la iglesia y cómo fue la relación de los cristianos con el gobierno de su tiempo. Meditemos seriamente si podemos hacer más bien involucrándonos en la política, especialmente en el proceso de votación. O si Dios quiere que oremos por nuestros funcionarios electos, que los veamos como sus siervos y que hablemos de ellos con respeto. En última instancia, debemos confiar en que Dios traerá a cabo su voluntad para el transcurso del “reloj del tiempo” conforme el tiempo avanza hacia el fin. Dios hará esto endureciendo los corazones de hombres impíos en posiciones de poder, tal como lo hizo con el Faraón de antaño, para cumplir su soberana voluntad para el mundo.

Entonces, ¿cuál es la solución cuando luchamos en nuestro interior por la dirección de nuestro país y su creciente inestabilidad o cuando sentimos tanta presión de nuestros pares o de la sociedad para involucrarnos y hacer la diferencia? El apóstol Pablo nos da una dirección muy clara cuando dice: Exhorto, pues, ante todo, que se hagan peticiones, oraciones, intercesiones y acciones de gracias, por todos los hombres; por los reyes y por todos los que están en eminencia, para que vivamos quieta y reposadamente en toda piedad y honestidad. —1 Timoteo 2:1-2. El poder secreto de influencia del cristiano yace en el poder de la oración que se produce en la privacidad de su aposento. Sin embargo, para que esta oración tenga poder debe nacer de un corazón de fe —Y Jesús les dijo… De cierto os digo, si tenéis fe como un grano de mostaza, diréis a este monte: Pásate de aquí allá, y se pasará; y nada os será imposible —Mateo 17:20. Recordemos siempre que …la oración eficaz y ferviente del justo puede mucho —Santiago 5:16.

Hasta la próxima, que Dios esté con cada uno y les conceda gracia y paz mientras caminan fielmente conforme a su Palabra. Oremos los unos por los otros mientras atravesamos los tiempos difíciles en nuestro mundo hoy.

Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created –Revelation 4:11.

This hymn, often called the “National Anthem of Christendom,” is perhaps one of the greatest of hymns of all time. It was written by Edward Perronet, first appearing in the November 1779 issue of Gospel Magazine. It was edited by Augustus Toplady, who is also the author of another well-known hymn, “Rock of Ages”. The text of this hymn, All Hail the Power of Jesus Name, has been translated into almost every language where Christianity is known. Wherever it is sung, it communicates to the spiritual needs of human hearts. One writer has said, “So long as there are Christians on earth, it will continue to be sung; and after that, in heaven.”

Edward Perronet was born at Sundridge, Kent, England, in 1726. He was a descendant of a distinguished French Huguenot family who had fled to Switzerland and later to England because of the religious persecution in France. Edward’s father, a pastor in the State Church of England, was strongly sympathetic with the evangelical movement spearheaded by the Wesleys and George Whitefield. Edward, too, like his father, became a minister in the Anglican Church but was always critical of its ways. Once he wrote, “I was born and I am likely to die in the tottering communion of the Church of England, but I despise her nonsense.” Soon, however, he broke from the Church and threw himself strenuously into the evangelistic endeavors of the Wesleys during the 1740s and 1750s.

Charles Wesley writes of Edward Perronet’s boldness in preaching. At one time he and Perronet were beset in a house by a mob of rough revilers, whom Perronet opposed courageously, while they abused him and threw dirt on him. It was during this time that the Wesleys and their followers suffered much persecution and even violence from those who disagreed with their ministry. Concerning these experiences, Wesley made the following notation in his diary: “From Rockdale we went to Bolton, and soon found that the Rockdale lions were lambs in comparison with those of Bolton.” Edward Perronet was thrown down and rolled in mud and mire. Stones were hurled and windows broken.

Another interesting account is given regarding the relationship between the Wesleys and Perronet. John Wesley wanted to hear Perronet preach, and he, being 18 years younger than John had always refused to preach in the older churchman’s presence. So, one day Wesley seeing Edward in the congregation announced that he would preach at the next service. Desiring to avoid a public conflict with Wesley, Perronet mounted the pulpit the next morning, but quickly explained that he had never consented to preach. “However,” he added, “I shall deliver the greatest sermon that has ever been preached on earth.” He then read the Sermon on the Mount and sat down without comment.

After eight years of co-operation with the Wesleys, Perronet’s strong-mindedness and free spirit caused a division between them, as he disagreed with some of their regulations. They continued, however, to esteem and love each other.

The last years of Perronet were spent at Canterbury, where he was pastor of an independent church, and where he died in 1792, at the age of sixty-six. His last words have also become a classic: “Glory to God in the height of His divinity! Glory to God in the depth of His humanity! Glory to God in His all-sufficiency! Into His hands I commend my spirit.”

Though Perronet wrote many other hymns and forms of poetry, none of them, have attained fame except the immortal “All Hail the Power of Jesus Name.” The success of this text has, no doubt, been furthered by three fine tunes. “Coronation,” composed by Oliver Holden, a Massachusetts carpenter, self-taught musician, and respected singing-school teacher, is most widely used in America. “Miles Lane” composed by William Shrubsole, Perronet’s personal friend, is the most popular in Great Britain. While the festive “Diadem” tune, composed in 1838 for this text by James Ellor, an English layman, is frequently used as a choir number. This hymn was originally written having the title, “On the Resurrection,” and there were eight stanzas, as follows:

All hail the power of Jesus’ name,
Let angels prostrate fall
Bring forth the royal diadem,
To crown Him Lord of all!

Let high born seraphs tune the lyre,
And, as they tune it, fall
Before His face who tunes their choir,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye morning stars of light,
Who fixed this floating ball,
Now hail the Strength of Israel’s might,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God,
Who from His altar call;
Extol the stem of Jesse’s rod,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Ye seed of Israel’s chosen race,
Ye ransomed of the fall,
Hail Him who saves you by His grace
And crown Him Lord of all!

Hail Him, ye heirs of David’s line,
Whom David Lord did call.
The God incarnate, Man divine,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Sinners, whose love can ne’er forget
The wormwood and the gall,
Go spread your trophies at His feet,
And crown Him Lord of all!

Let every tribe and every tongue
That bound creation’s call
Now shout in universal song,
The crowned Lord of all!

As it now stands in our hymnbooks, the hymn is shortened and changed, and one stanza has been added by the famous hymn collector, Rev. John Rippon, in 1787.

Oh, that with yonder sacred throng
We at His feet may fall;
We’ll join the everlasting song,
And crown Him Lord of all.

As we wrap up this amazing story of the life of Edward Perronet and the others who have had their part in bringing this immortal hymn to us, let’s take a look in closing at the effect this hymn has had on heathens who knew nothing about Jesus. The most famous story connected with Perronet’s great hymn is told of the missionary to India, Rev. E.P. Scott. One day he saw on the street a man of so strange an appearance that he inquired about him and learned that he belonged to a wild mountain tribe among whom Christ had never been preached. Mr. Scott prayed over the matter and decided to visit that tribe. As soon as he reached their mountain home, he fell in among a savage band of murderous tribesmen who were on a war expedition, and who were closing in on him with their spears. They seized him and pointed their spears at his heart. At once the missionary drew out the violin that he always carried with him and began to play and sing in the native language, “All hail the power of Jesus’ name!” He closed his eyes, expecting death at any minute. When he reached the fourth stanza, and nothing had happened, he opened his eyes, and was amazed to see that the spears had fallen from the hands of the savages, and big tears were in their eyes! They invited Mr. Scott to their homes, and he spent the remaining years of his life preaching and ministering God’s love and redemption to these people. God in His providence used a simple hymn as a means of introducing the gospel to a group of needy pagans.

101 Hymn stories

“Miles Lane” Tune -William Shrubsole, 1760-1806
“Diadem” Tune -James Elliot, 1838
“Let Us Crown Him” Tune -James McGranahan 1840-1907

তুমি যোগ্য, হে প্রভু, মহিমা ও সম্মান ও ক্ষমতা গ্রহণ করতে; কারণ তুমি সমস্ত বস্তু সৃষ্টি করেছ; এবং তাদের লক্ষ্যার্থে তারা আছে এবং ছিল—প্রকাশিতবাক্য ৪:১১।

এই পদ্যটি, যা প্রায়ই “খ্রীষ্টানদের জাতীয় সংগীত” বলে ডাকা হয়, সম্ভবত সবসময়ের অন্যতম শ্রেষ্ঠ স্তবগীত। এটি লিখেছিলেন Edward Perronet, প্রথমবার প্রকাশ পেয়েছিল Gospel Magazine-এর ১৭৭৯ সালের নভেম্বর সংখ্যায়। এটি সম্পাদনা করেছিলেন Augustus Toplady, যিনি আরেকটি পরিচিত স্তবগীত “Rock of Ages”-এর রচয়িতা। এই স্তবগীতটির পাঠ, All Hail the Power of Jesus Name, এমন প্রায় প্রতিটি ভাষায় অনূদিত হয়েছে যেখানে খ্রিস্টধর্ম পরিচিত। যেখানে এটিকে গাওয়া হয়, এটি মানুষের হৃদয়ের আধ্যাত্মিক চাহিদার সঙ্গে কথা বলে। এক লেখক বলেছেন, “যতক্ষণ পৃথিবীতে খ্রিস্টান থাকবে, এটি চালু থাকবে; এবং এর পর, স্বর্গে।”

Edward Perronet ১৭২৬ সালে সানড্রিজ, কেন্ট, ইংল্যান্ডে জন্মগ্রহণ করেন। তিনি এক বিশিষ্ট ফরাসি হুগেনট বংশের সন্তান ছিলেন, যারা ফ্রান্সে ধর্মীয় নির্যাতনের ফলে সুইজারল্যান্ডে পালিয়ে গিয়ে পরে ইংল্যান্ডে এসেছিলেন। Edward-এর পিতা, ইংল্যান্ডের রাষ্ট্রীয় চার্চের একজন পাদ্রি, ওয়েসলিদের এবং জর্জ হোয়াইটফিল্ডের নেতৃত্বাধীন evangelical আন্দোলনের প্রতি গভীর সহানুভূতিশীল ছিলেন। Edward-ও, পিতার মতো, অ্যাঙ্গ্লিকান চার্চে একজন মন্ত্রী হয়েছিলেন, কিন্তু তিনি সবসময় তার উপায়-উপকরণ নিয়ে সমালোচিত ছিলেন। একবার তিনি লিখেছিলেন, “আমি জন্মেছি এবং আমি সম্ভবত অ্যাঙ্গেলিকান চার্চের দোলাখোলা ঐক্যর মাঝে মরব, কিন্তু আমি তার বাজে কথা তুচ্ছ মনে করি।” ততক্ষণে তিনি চার্চ থেকে বিচ্ছিন্ন হয়ে ওঠেন এবং ১৭৪০ ও ১৭৫০-এর দশকে ওয়েসলিদের প্রচারকর্মে কঠোরভাবে জড়িয়ে পড়েন।

Charles Wesley Edward Perronet-এর সাহসিক প্রচারের কথা বর্ণনা করেছেন। এক সময় তিনি এবং Perronet এক বাড়িতে ভাঙচুরকারী উল্লাসকারীদের দ্বারা আক্রমণাত্মক অবহেলায় পড়েছিলেন, যাদের বিরুদ্ধে Perronet সাহসিকতার সঙ্গে বিরোধিতা করেছিলেন, এবং তারা তাকে গালিগালাজ করে মাটি ছিটকে দিয়েছিল। এ সময় ওয়েসলিরা এবং তাদের অনুসারীরা অনেক নির্যাতন এবং এমনকি সহিংসতা ভোগ করেছিলেন তাদের সেবার প্রতি বিভক্তদের কাছ থেকে। এসব অভিজ্ঞতা সম্পর্কে Wesley তাঁর ডায়রিতে নোট করেছেন: “রকডেল থেকে আমরা বলটনে গেলাম, এবং দেখা গেল রকডেলের সিংহরা বলটনের সিংহদের তুলনায় বেশি ভয়াবহ ছিল।” Edward Perronetকে মাটিতে ফেলে মাটি ও কাদায় রুব করা হয়েছিল। পাথর নিক্ষেপ করা হয় এবং জানালা ভাঙা হয়।

ওয়েসলিদের এবং Perronet-এর সম্পর্ক সম্পর্কে আরেকটি আকর্ষণীয় বিবরণ আছে। John Wesley Perronet-এর বক্তৃতা শুনতে চেয়েছিলেন, এবং Perronet, যিনি John-এর চেয়ে ১৮ বছর নবীন, সবসময় বুড়ো চার্চম্যানের উপস্থিতিতে ভাষণ দিতে অস্বীকার করতেন। তাই একদিন Wesley জনসভায় Edward-কে দেখে ঘোষণা করলেন তিনি পরের সেবায় বক্তৃতা দেবেন। জনসমক্ষে Wesley-এর সঙ্গে বিবাদ এড়াতে চাইতেথ Perronet পরের সকালে pulpitte উঠলেন, কিন্তু দ্রুত ব্যাখ্যা করলেন যে তিনি কখনো বক্তৃতা দিতে সম্মত হননি। “তবু,” তিনি যোগ করলেন, “আমি পৃথিবীতে দেওয়া সর্ববৃহৎ ধর্মপ্রচার করব।” তারপর তিনি প্রচারনাসূত্রিক বক্তব্য—পর্বতবক্তৃতা—পড়লেন এবং কোন ব্যাখ্যা না দিয়ে নেমে এলেন।

ওয়েসলিদের সঙ্গে আট বছর সহযোগিতার পর, Perronet-এর দৃঢ় মনস্তত্ত্ব ও স্বাধীন আত্মচেতনা তাদের মধ্যে বিভাজন সৃষ্টি করেছিল, কারণ তিনি তাদের কিছু নিয়মের সঙ্গে অসম্মত ছিলেন। তবু তারা একে অপরকে সম্মান ও ভক্তি প্রদর্শন করে যেতে থাকলেন।

Perronet-এর শেষ বছরগুলো ক্যান্টারবেরিতে কেটেছিল, যেখানে তিনি একটি স্বাধীন চার্চের পাদ্রি ছিলেন, এবং যেখানে তিনি ১৭৯২ সালে ছেষট্টি বছর বয়সে মৃত্যুবরণ করেন। তাঁর শেষ কথাগুলোও কিংবদন্তির মতো হয়ে উঠেছে: “ঈশ্বরের ঐশ্বর্য্য উচ্চতায় মহিমা! মানবতার গভীরে ঈশ্বরের মহিমা! তাঁর পরিপূর্ণতায় ঈশ্বরের মহিমা! তাঁর হাতে আমি আমার আত্মা অর্পণ করি।”

Perronet বহু অন্যান্য স্তবগীত ও কবিতা লিখেছিলেন, তবু তাদের মধ্যে কোনোটিই অমর “All Hail the Power of Jesus Name” ছাড়া খ্যাতি পায়নি। এই পাঠের সাফল্য নিঃসন্দেহে তিনটি চমৎকার সুরের কারণে আরও বাড়ে। “Coronation,” রচিত Oliver Holden দ্বারা, যিনি মাসাচুসেটসের একজন চাকরশিল্পী, স্বশিক্ষিত সঙ্গীতজ্ঞ এবং প্রখ্যাত গানশালা শিক্ষক, আমেরিকায় সবচেয়ে প্রচলিত। “Miles Lane” রচিত William Shrubsole দ্বারা, Perronet-এর ব্যক্তিগত বন্ধু, গ্রেট ব্রিটেনে সবচেয়ে জনপ্রিয়। উৎসবমুখর “Diadem” সুরটি, ১৮৩৮ সালে James Ellor নামক একজন ইংরেজ layman-এর দ্বারা এই পাঠের জন্য রচিত, প্রায়শই কোরাল সংখ্যা হিসেবে ব্যবহৃত হয়। এই স্তবগীতটি মূলত “পুনরুত্থানের উপর” শিরোনামে রচিত হয়েছিল এবং এতে আট স্তবক ছিল, নিম্নরূপ:

যীশুর নামে সকল শক্তিকে সম্ভাষণ করো,
দেবদূতেরা নতপ্রণাম করুক;
আনো রাজার প্রাসাদীন মুকুটটি,
যাতে তাঁকে সকলের প্রভু হিসেবে সজ্জিত করা যায়!

উচ্চ জন্মারম্ভী সারাফদেরকে বীণায় সুর বাঁধতে বলো,
আর সুর বাঁধলে তারা নতপ্রণাম করবে;
তাঁর সম্মুখে যিনি তাদের গায়কের দলকে সুর দেন—তার সম্মুখে নত হও,
এবং তাঁকে সকলের প্রভু মানও!

তাঁকে মুকুট পরাও, হে প্রভাতের তারা,
যিনি এই ভাসমান গৃহটিকে স্থির রেখেছো;
এখন নিরাপত্তার শক্তিকে অভিবাদন করো ইস্রায়েলের বল,
এবং তাঁকে সকলের প্রভু হিসেবে মুকুট পরাও!

তোমাদের প্রভুর জন্যে, হে শহীদগণ, মুকুট পরাও,
যাঁরা তাঁর বলকের সম্মুখ থেকে ডাক পেয়েছো;
যেসির লাঠির শেকড়কে উচ্চকিত করো,
এবং তাঁকে সকলের প্রভু হিসেবে মুকুট পরাও!

তোমরা ইস্রায়েলের নির্বাচিত বংশের বীজ,
পতন থেকে মুক্তির জন্য উদ্ধারপ্রাপ্তরা,
তাঁর কৃপায় তোমাদের রক্ষা করার তাঁকে স্বাগত জানাও,
এবং তাঁকে সকলের প্রভু হিসেবে মুকুট পরাও!

তাঁকে অভিবাদন করো, হে দাভিদের বংশের উত্তরাধিকারেরা,
যাকে দাভিদ প্রভু বলে ডেকেছিলো;
অবতারকৃত ঈশ্বর, মানব হয়ে দীপ্তিমান—
তাঁকে সকলের প্রভু হিসেবে মুকুট পরাও!

পাপীরা, যাদের প্রেম কখনও ভুলে যেতে পারে না
কষ্ঠকাণ্ড ও করাল বাষ্প—
তোমরা তোমাদের বিজয়চিহ্ন তাঁর পায়ের তলে ছড়িয়ে দাও,
এবং তাঁকে সকলের প্রভু হিসেবে মুকুট পরাও!

হোক প্রতিটি কুল ও প্রতিটি ভাষা—
যারা সৃষ্টির কর্তব্যে আবদ্ধ ছিল—
এখন সর্বজনীন গান গেয়ে উল্লাস করো,
সিংহাসনে আরোপিত প্রভুকে সমুচ্চারণ করো!

আমাদের স্তবগীতগ্রন্থে যে রূপে আছে, সেই রীতি অনুযায়ী এই স্তবগীতটি সংক্ষিপ্ত ও পরিবর্তিত হয়েছে, এবং এক স্তবক ১৭৮৭ সালে বিখ্যাত স্তবগীত সংগ্রাহক Rev. John Rippon দ্বারা যোগ করা হয়েছে।

ওহ, যে পবিত্র সমাবেশে আমরা রয়েছি—
আমরা তাঁর পায়ে নত হতে পারি সেখানেই;
আমরা অনন্ত গীতের সাথে মিলিত হবো,
এবং তাঁকে সকলের প্রভু হিসেবে মুকুট পরাবো।

Edward Perronet-এর জীবনকাহিনী ও এই অমর স্তবগীত আমাদের কাছে পৌঁছানোর পথে যারা অংশগ্রহণ করেছিলেন তাদের কাহিনী শেষ করার সময়, চলুন শেষটায় দেখি যে এই স্তবগীত কুসংস্কারমুক্ত যারা যীশুকে জানেন না তাদের উপর কী প্রভাব ফেলেছে। Perronet-এর মহান স্তবগীতের সঙ্গে সবচেয়ে বিখ্যাত কাহিনী ভারতীয় মিশনারি Rev. E.P. Scott-র কথা বলে। একদিন তিনি রাস্তায় এমন এক ব্যক্তিকে দেখেন যার চেহারা এত অদ্ভুত ছিল যে তিনি তার সম্পর্কে জিজ্ঞাসা করে জানতে পারেন যে তিনি একটি বন্য পার্বত্য উপজাতির সদস্য, যেখানে খ্রীষ্ট কখনো প্রচারিত হয়নি। Mr. Scott এই বিষয় নিয়ে প্রার্থনা করেন এবং ওই উপজাতি পরিদর্শনে সিদ্ধান্ত নেন। তিনি পৌঁছতেই একটি নির্মম যুদ্ধগোষ্ঠীর সঙ্গে তিনি পড়ে যান, যে দলটি একটি যুদ্ধ অভিযানে ছিল এবং তার দিকে শাস্র নিয়ে এগোচ্ছিল। তারা তাকে ধরাধরি করে এবং তাদের শাস্র তাঁর অন্তঃকরণে নিশানা করল। সঙ্গে সঙ্গে মিশনারি তাঁর সঙ্গে থাকা বায়োলিন বের করে আনলেন এবং দেশীয় ভাষায় গাইতে শুরু করলেন, “All hail the power of Jesus’ name!” তিনি চোখ বন্ধ করে ছিলেন, মনে করে প্রতিটি মুহূর্তেই মৃত্যু আসতে পারে। যখন তিনি চতুর্থ স্তবক পৌঁছালেন এবং কিছু ঘটল না, তিনি চোখ খুলে দেখলেন বিস্ময়ে যে আক্রমণকারীদের হাতে থাকা শাস্রগুলি পড়ে গেছে, এবং তাদের চোখে বড় বড় অশ্রু জ্বলছে! তারা Mr. Scott-কে তাদের বাড়িতে আমন্ত্রণ জানাল এবং তিনি জীবনের বাকি বছরগুলো সেই লোকদের কাছে ঈশ্বরের প্রেম ও মুক্তির বার্তা প্রচার এবং সেবা করতে কাটালেন। ঈশ্বর তাঁর প্রবর্তনায় একটি সরল স্তবগীতকে এমন একটি মাধ্যম হিসেবে ব্যবহার করলেন যা প্রয়োজনমতো পাগানদের কাছে সুসমাচার পরিচয় করিয়ে দিল।

And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. And they straightway left their nets, and followed him. And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them. And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him –Matthew 4:18-22.

Little did they know where this journey would lead them. They received the call, they responded to the call, and now they were on a journey that would forever change their lives. Little do we know when we choose to follow Jesus where that journey will lead us. That is why it is considered a journey of faith.

One thing is certain, walking with Jesus will lead you into a life of holiness. What exactly do we mean by holiness? Holiness is the full sum of the righteousness of Jesus manifested in our lives by the work of regeneration and the inner renewing of the Holy Ghost.

John the Baptist said of Jesus: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire –Matthew 3:11-12.

This speaks of the baptism of the Holy Ghost and fire, and of the thorough purging that Jesus would bring. Jesus did not come with violence and yet His righteous presence swept through Palestine like a winnowing breeze. Those who rejected Him were blown away and disappeared from the narrative. Those who loved Him were set forth as the chosen ones who became the founders of a new kingdom established on principles not known before.

The principles of this new kingdom are demonstrated in the life of Christ and explained in His teachings. In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus set forth teaching that challenged the most pious Pharisee and disturbed the apathy of the sinner. Jesus’ teachings were such that they could not be lightly ignored for they stirred a deep longing in the human heart for the love and peace that they offered while at the same time exposing the innate selfishness that prevented it.

It was this promise and hope of a new humanity that drew crowds of people after Him. They followed Jesus, some hoping for a miracle, some for bread, but many were drawn to Him by a deep inner longing for deliverance from the stranglehold of sin. Those who truly sought deliverance, found it.

One such disciple was Mary Magdalene. The Scripture gives us only cursory glances of her life. She appears to have been one of several women of whom the Scriptures make mention that followed Jesus. Doctor Luke tells us that Jesus healed her of evil spirits and infirmities. Apparently, she was not only possessed of evil spirits, but also physically infirmed.

And it came to pass afterward, that he went throughout every city and village, preaching and shewing the glad tidings of the kingdom of God: and the twelve were with him, And certain women, which had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils, And Joanna the wife of Chuza Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance –Luke 8:1-3.

Mary became a faithful follower of Jesus. Her presence is especially noted in the Scriptures after the death of Christ. She was first to the sepulcher early on the resurrection morning and she lingered there when the others had gone away. Her diligent pursuit of Christ was rewarded when Jesus appeared first to her.

Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away. Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master –John 20:15-16.

Mary knew Jesus the moment He spoke her name. This intimacy was born of a passion for Christ that was the fruit of her deliverance. Mary’s love for Jesus was the result of having been delivered from seven devils.

Jesus’ primary mission in coming to earth was to deliver us from the power of sin. In Luke 5, Doctor Luke records an account of a man who was paralyzed. He could not walk. His friends brought him for healing, but they could not reach Jesus because of the crowd. So, they went up onto the roof and removed enough of roof tiles to let their friend through and lowered him into the presence of Jesus. How ingenious! How desperate they were to help their friend to find healing.

And when he saw their faith, he said unto him, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee –Luke 5:20. They sought healing, but Jesus saw the deeper need of this man’s soul, so He offered forgiveness. This, of course, raised the ire of the Pharisees who …began to reason, saying, Who is this which speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone? –Luke 5:21. They were right, only God can forgive sins, but what they did not want to believe was that Jesus was God’s Son and that thus He had did have the power to forgive sins. So, Jesus went on to say: …What reason ye in your hearts? Whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Rise up and walk? But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power upon earth to forgive sins, (he said unto the sick of the palsy,) I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy couch, and go into thine house –Luke 5:22-24.

To follow Jesus is to leave your sins. We would be greatly mistaken to suggest that holiness is a product of human effort. Our journey to holiness must be a journey to Calvary. Many “holy men” and “holy women” down through the ages have sought to live a holy life in their own strength. What always happens is that we settle for a form of godliness that falls short of Christ’s righteousness. We settle for a religion that is doable.

The apostle Paul, when writing about his Jewish brethren said: For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God –Romans 10:3.

This “righteousness of God” is an inner righteousness of the heart that can only come about through the work of regeneration and the renewing of the Holy Ghost. It is for this reason that our journey with Jesus must lead us to Calvary for it is there that we behold our dying Lord—bleeding, dying for our sins—for my sins—for your sins.

The blood of Jesus is the only means to the “righteousness of God”. The “righteousness of God” is imputed through forgiveness, and it is the fruit of our lives after being empowered through the Holy Spirit. Either way, the “righteousness of God” is attributed to the work of Christ on the cross. There is no other means to holiness.

In Mathew 22, Jesus told the story of a king who planned a wedding for his son. When the invited guests (the Jewish people) refused his invitation, the invitation then went out to all those who had not been invited, and the wedding was furnished with guests.

When the king came in to observe the wedding, he was pleased with what he saw until he spotted a man who was not wearing a wedding garment. (A wedding garment was a white linen garment that was provided by the master of the feast.)

I quote Adam Clark: “Among the Orientals, long white robes were worn at public festivals; and those who appeared on such occasions with any other garments were esteemed, not only highly culpable, but worthy of punishment. The person who invited the guests prepared such a garment for each, for the time being; and with which he was furnished on his application to the ruler of the feast. It was this which made the conduct of the person mentioned in the text inexcusable; he might have had a proper marriage garment, if he had applied for it”.

“Not wearing a wedding garment” was to insult the master of the feast, who provided everything, (including the wedding garment) so that all the guests would be equally suited for the occasion. No one needs to be excluded for lack of proper clothing or any other amenity. The king provided the invitation and all necessary amenities, and the guest need only to accept the invitation and receive the gracious provision of the king.

What a beautiful analogy of the Kingdom of Heaven. The King has invited us to His heavenly feast. He wants us to come and enjoy the feast with Him. He wants us to come no matter who we are or where we come from—some from the gutters of sin, some from the depth of ignorance, and some from the temples of self-righteousness. All are invited to come on equal terms—All must accept the invitation, and all must wear the wedding garment.

We are not told the exact condition of this man who refused the wedding garment, but a general understanding of human nature would indicate that he was probably a well-dressed gentleman. Those who came shabbily dressed would have welcomed the wedding garment to disguise their true condition. Most likely this man wanted to display his finery. He did not feel inclined to cover his fine clothing with a simple white cloak.

This is the condition of all who trust in their own righteousness. The best that we can bring to God falls short of the righteousness that God requires. Isaiah wrote: But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away –Isaiah 64:6.

In this desperate situation we find ourselves in need of a redeemer. God has provided us with a Redeemer in His Son, Jesus. In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace –Ephesians 1:7. God has invited us to His feast, and He has provided us with everything that is needed that we can be made righteous.

One attribute of a person who has been cleansed from sin through the blood of Christ, is worship. Luke tells the story of a woman who “was a sinner” who came to worship Jesus: And, behold, a woman in the city, which was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at meat in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster box of ointment, And stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment. Now when the Pharisee which had bidden him saw it, he spake within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him: for she is a sinner –Luke 7:37-39.

We do not know her name, only that she “was a sinner”. That was her reputation—she was ‘not good’. But she apparently had had a previous encounter with Jesus. She came to Simon’s house to offer her sacrifice of thanksgiving. She brought the best that she had. An alabaster box of ointment said to have been worth a year’s wages. She anointed Jesus’ feet and washed them with her tears—tears of repentance, tears of joy, tears of relief.

Simon observed her worship. He despised her in his heart. He considered her offering a great waste. Jesus challenged him. He said to Simon: …Seest thou this woman? I entered into thine house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head. Thou gavest me no kiss: but this woman since the time I came in hath not ceased to kiss my feet. My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but this woman hath anointed my feet with ointment. Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little –Luke 7:44-47.

He said to the woman …Thy sins are forgiven –Luke 7:48. Forgiveness, and freedom from sin, awaken the heart to worship. When a man or woman is set free from the guilt and bondage of sin, praise flows freely. Simon was a Pharisee who was relying on his own righteousness. Yet Jesus brought him to the awareness that he was greatly lacking in love and worship.

Following Jesus will lead us to holiness of heart and life. Following Jesus brings us face to face with the cause and the cure of the sin problem. The cause of sin is our fallen carnal nature, and our fallen nature is revealed in the light of His holiness. Along with Mary Magdalene and the other disciples, as we journey with Jesus, we become aware of our need and our need cries out for His grace. The cure for our sin is Jesus—…thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins –Matthew 1:21.

In Augustus Toplady’s famous hymn, Rock of Ages we find this line–

Be of sin the double cure; save me from its guilt (through forgiveness) and power (through sanctification).

Og Jesus, vandrende ved Galileas sjø, så to brødre, Simon som kalles Peter, og Andreas hans bror, kaste et garn i sjøen; for de var fiskere. Og han sier til dem: Følg meg, og jeg vil gjøre dere til menneskefiskere. Og de forlot straks garnene og fulgte ham. Og da han gikk derfra, så han to andre brødre, Jakob, Zebedeus' sønn, og Johannes hans bror, i et skip sammen med Zebedeus deres far, som reparerte garnene; og han kalte dem. Og de forlot straks skipet og sin far og fulgte ham – Matteus 4:18-22.

Lite visste de hvor denne vandringen ville føre dem. De mottok kallet, de svarte på kallet, og nå var de på en reise som for alltid ville forandre livet deres. Lite vet vi når vi velger å følge Jesus hvor den reisen vil føre oss. Derfor regnes det som en vandring i tro.

Én ting er sikkert: å vandre med Jesus vil føre deg inn i et liv i hellighet. Hva mener vi egentlig med hellighet? Hellighet er den fulle summen av Jesu rettferdighet som manifesteres i våre liv ved gjenfødelsens verk og den indre fornyelse ved Den Hellige Ånd.

Johannes døperen sa om Jesus: Jeg døyper dere med vann til omvendelse; men han som kommer etter meg er sterkere enn jeg, så jeg eier ikke engang kraft til å løse hans sko; han skal døpe dere med Den Hellige Ånd og med ild. Hans vifte er i hans hånd, og han skal gjennomtrenge sin åker og samle sitt korn i låven; men agnet skal han brenne opp med en ild som ikke kan slukkes – Matteus 3:11-12.

Dette taler om dåpen med Den Hellige Ånd og ild, og om den grundige rensing som Jesus skulle bringe. Jesus kom ikke med vold, og likevel feide Hans rettferdige nærvær over Palestina som en vind som skiller agnet fra kornet. De som avviste ham ble blåst bort og forsvant fra beretningen. De som elsket ham ble framhevet som de utvalgte som ble grunnleggere av et nytt rike etablert på prinsipper som ikke var kjent før.

Prinsippene i dette nye riket blir demonstrert i Kristi liv og forklart i hans lære. I Bergprekenen framla Jesus en lære som utfordret den mest fromme fariseer og forstyrret den syndiges likegyldighet. Jesu lære var slik at den ikke kunne ignoreres lett, for den vekk en dyp lengsel i menneskets hjerte etter den kjærlighet og fred den tilbød, samtidig som den avdekket den medfødte egoisme som hindret dette.

Det var dette løftet og dette håpet om et nytt menneske som dro folkemengder etter ham. De fulgte Jesus, noen i håp om et under, noen etter brød, men mange ble trukket til ham av en dyp indre lengsel etter forløsning fra syndens grep. De som virkelig søkte forløsning fant den.

En slik disippel var Maria Magdalena. Skriften gir oss bare korte glimt av hennes liv. Hun synes å ha vært en av flere kvinner som Skriftene nevner som fulgte Jesus. Lukas skriver at Jesus helbredet henne fra onde ånder og sykdommer. Tilsynelatende var hun ikke bare besatt av onde ånder, men også fysisk syk.

Og det hendte etter dette at han gikk omkring i alle byer og landsbyer og forkynte og forkynte Guds rike; og de tolv var med ham, og visse kvinner som var blitt helbredet fra onde ånder og sykdommer, Maria kalt Magdalena, av hvem det gikk ut syv demoner, og Johanna, Chuza Herodes' forvalters hustru, og Susanna, og mange andre, som betjente ham av sine midler – Lukas 8:1-3.

Maria ble en trofast følger av Jesus. Hennes nærvær blir spesielt nevnt i Skriften etter Kristi død. Hun var den første ved graven tidlig på oppstandelsens morgen, og hun ble værende der da de andre var gått bort. Hennes nidkjære søken etter Kristus ble belønnet da Jesus viste seg først for henne.

Jesus sa til henne: «Kvinne, hvorfor gråter du? Hvem søker du?» Hun, som trodde han var gartneren, sa til ham: «Herre, har du båret ham bort, si meg hvor du har lagt ham, og jeg vil ta ham bort.» Jesus sa til henne: «Maria.» Hun vendte seg og sa til ham: «Rabbuni», det vil si: Mester – Johannes 20:15-16.

Maria kjente Jesus i det øyeblikk han uttalte navnet hennes. Denne nærheten var født av en lidenskap for Kristus som var frukten av hennes forløsning. Marias kjærlighet til Jesus var resultatet av at hun var blitt fri fra syv demoner.

Jesu hovedoppdrag ved å komme til jorden var å befri oss fra syndens makt. I Lukas 5 gjengir Lukas en beretning om en lam mann. Han kunne ikke gå. Hans venner brakte ham for helbredelse, men de kom ikke fram til Jesus på grunn av folkemengden. Så gikk de opp på taket, fjernet nok av takteglene til å få vennen ned og senket ham ned foran Jesus. Hvor oppfinnsomme! Hvor desperate var de for å hjelpe vennen å finne helbredelse.

Og da han så deres tro, sa han til ham: «Mann, dine synder er forlatt deg» – Lukas 5:20. De søkte helbredelse, men Jesus så denne mannens dypere behov i sjelen, derfor tilbød han tilgivelse. Dette vekket selvsagt fariseernes harme som …begynte å tenke og si: Hvem er dette som taler blasfemi? Hvem kan tilgi synder uten Gud alene? – Lukas 5:21. De hadde rett; bare Gud kan tilgi synder, men det de ikke ville tro var at Jesus var Guds Sønn og at han dermed hadde myndighet til å tilgi synder. Derfor sa Jesus videre: …Hva tenker dere i deres hjerter? Hva er lettere å si: «Dine synder er forlatt deg», eller å si: «Stå opp og gå»? Men for at dere skal forstå at Menneskesønnen har myndighet på jorden til å tilgi synder, (sa han til den lamme,) sier jeg deg: Stå opp, ta din seng og gå hjem til ditt hus – Lukas 5:22-24.

Å følge Jesus er å forlate dine synder. Vi ville ta feil om vi påsto at hellighet er et produkt av menneskelig anstrengelse. Vår vandring mot hellighet må være en vandring til Golgata. Mange «fromme menn» og «fromme kvinner» gjennom tidene har forsøkt å leve et hellig liv i egen kraft. Hva som alltid skjer er at vi nøyer oss med en form for gudsfrykt som faller kort for Kristi rettferdighet. Vi nøyer oss med en religion som er gjennomførbar.

Apostelen Paulus, da han skrev om sine jødiske brødre, sa: For de, som ikke kjenner Guds rettferdighet, og som forsøker å opprette sin egen rettferdighet, har ikke underkastet seg Guds rettferdighet – Romerne 10:3.

Denne «Guds rettferdighet» er en indre rettferdighet i hjertet som bare kan komme gjennom gjenfødelsens verk og Den Hellige Ånds fornyelse. Det er av denne grunn at vår vandring med Jesus må føre oss til Golgata, for det er der vi ser vår døende Herre—blødende, døende for våre synder—for mine synder—for dine synder.

Jesu blod er det eneste middel til «Guds rettferdighet». «Guds rettferdighet» tilregnes gjennom tilgivelse, og den blir frukten av våre liv etter å ha blitt styrket ved Den Hellige Ånd. Uansett hvordan, tilregnes «Guds rettferdighet» Kristi verk på korset. Det finnes intet annet middel til hellighet.

I Matteus 22 fortalte Jesus lignelsen om en konge som planla et bryllup for sin sønn. Da de innbudne gjestene (det jødiske folket) nektet invitasjonen, gikk invitasjonen ut til alle dem som ikke var innbudt, og bryllupet ble fylt med gjester.

Når kongen gikk inn for å se på bryllupet, var han tilfreds med det han så inntil han fikk øye på en mann som ikke hadde på seg bryllupsklær. (Et bryllupsklede var et hvitt linplagg som var tilveiebrakt av verten.)

Jeg siterer Adam Clark: «Blant orientalere ble lange hvite kjortler brukt ved offentlige fester; og de som viste seg på slike anledninger i andre klær ble ansett ikke bare som høyst klanderverdige, men verdige straff. Den som inviterte gjestene tilberedte et slikt plagg for hver, for tiden; og med det ble man utstyrt ved henvendelse til festens hersker. Det var dette som gjorde oppførselen til personen nevnt i teksten uforbederlig; han kunne ha mottatt et passende ekteskapsplagg, om han hadde søkt om det.»

«Å ikke ha på seg bryllupsklær» var en fornærmelse mot festens herre, som hadde sørget for alt (inkludert bryllupsklærne) slik at alle gjestene skulle være likt skikket for anledningen. Ingen skulle utelukkes for mangel på passende bekledning eller andre nødvendigheter. Kongen ga invitasjonen og alt som trengtes, og gjesten trengte bare å ta imot invitasjonen og motta kongens nådige forberedelse.

For et vakkert bilde på himmelriket. Kongen har invitert oss til sitt himmelske gjestebud. Han vil at vi skal komme og nyte festen sammen med ham. Han vil at vi skal komme uansett hvem vi er eller hvor vi kommer fra—noen fra syndens sluk, noen fra uvitenhetens mørke, og noen fra selvrettferdighetens templer. Alle er innbudt på like vilkår—alle må motta invitasjonen, og alle må bære bryllupsklærne.

Vi får ikke vite nøyaktig hva slags menneske denne som avslo bryllupsklær var, men en generell forståelse av menneskenaturen antyder at han trolig var en velkledd herre. De som kom dårlig kledd ville ha ønsket seg bryllupsklærne for å skjule sin sanne tilstand. Mest sannsynlig ønsket denne mannen å vise fram sin prakt. Han følte seg ikke tilbøyelig til å dekke sin fine drakt med en enkel hvit kappe.

Dette er tilstanden til alle som stoler på sin egen rettferdighet. Det beste vi kan bringe for Guds åsyn står tilbake for den rettferdighet Gud krever. Jesaja skrev: Men vi er alle som urene, og all vår rettferdighet er som en skitten klut; og vi visner alle som et blad; og våre misgjerninger, som vinden, fører oss bort – Jesaja 64:6.

I denne fortvilelse finner vi oss i behov for en Forløser. Gud har gitt oss en Forløser i sin Sønn, Jesus. I ham har vi forløsning ved hans blod, syndenes tilgivelse, etter rikdommen i hans nåde – Efeserne 1:7. Gud har invitert oss til sitt gjestebud, og han har gitt oss alt som trengs for at vi kan bli gjort rettferdige.

Et kjennetegn ved en person som er blitt renset fra synd ved Kristi blod, er tilbedelse. Lukas forteller om en kvinne som «var en synder» som kom for å tilbe Jesus: Se, en kvinne i byen som var en synder, da hun fikk høre at Jesus satt til bords i fariseerens hus, kom og tok et alabastkrukke med salve; og hun sto bak ham ved føttene og gråt, og begynte å vaske hans føtter med tårer, og tørket dem med sitt hår, og kysset hans føtter, og salvet dem med salven. Fariseeren som hadde innbudt ham så dette, og tenkte for seg selv: Denne mannen, om han var en profet, ville vite hvem denne kvinnen som rører ved ham er; for hun er en synder – Lukas 7:37-39.

Vi vet ikke navnet hennes, bare at hun «var en synder». Det var hennes rykte—hun var ‘ikke god’. Men hun hadde tydeligvis hatt et tidligere møte med Jesus. Hun kom til Simons hus for å bringe sitt takkoffer. Hun tok med det beste hun eide. En alabastkrukke med salve sies å ha vært verdt et års lønn. Hun salvet Jesu føtter og vasket dem med sine tårer—tårer av omvendelse, tårer av glede, tårer av lettelse.

Simon observerte hennes tilbedelse. Han foraktet henne i sitt hjerte. Han vurderte hennes offer som en stor sløsing. Jesus utfordret ham. Han sa til Simon: Ser du denne kvinnen? Jeg kom inn i ditt hus, du gav meg ikke vann til mine føtter; men hun har vasket mine føtter med tårer og tørket dem med sitt hår. Du gav meg ikke et kyss; men denne kvinnen har siden jeg kom inn ikke sluttet å kysse mine føtter. Mitt hode med olje salvet du ikke; men denne kvinnen har salvet mine føtter med salve. Derfor sier jeg deg: Hennes synder, som er mange, er tilgitt; for hun elsket meget. Men den som får liten tilgivelse, elsker lite – Lukas 7:44-47.

Han sa til kvinnen: …Dine synder er deg tilgitt – Lukas 7:48. Tilgivelse og frihet fra synd vekker hjertet til tilbedelse. Når en mann eller kvinne blir satt fri fra syndens skyld og trelldom, flyter lovprisning fritt. Simon var en fariseer som stolte på sin egen rettferdighet. Likevel førte Jesus ham til bevissthet om at han var stor i mangel på kjærlighet og tilbedelse.

Å følge Jesus vil føre oss til hellighet i hjerte og liv. Å følge Jesus bringer oss ansikt til ansikt med årsaken til og kuren for syndsproblemet. Årsaken til synd er vår falne kjødelige natur, og vår falne natur blir åpenbart i lyset av Hans hellighet. Sammen med Maria Magdalena og de andre disiplene, når vi vandrer med Jesus, blir vi klar over vårt behov, og vårt behov roper om Hans nåde. Kur for vår synd er Jesus—…du skal gi ham navnet JESUS: for han skal frelse sitt folk fra deres synder – Matteus 1:21.

I Augustus Topladys kjente salme, Rock of Ages (Klippens sal), finner vi denne linjen–

Vær syndens dobbelte medisin; frels meg fra dens skyld (ved tilgivelse) og dens makt (ved helliggjørelse).
